<a name="BooleanErrorCode"></a>
### type BooleanErrorCode

<pre>type BooleanErrorCode <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a></pre>

BooleanErrorCode is the branchable fine reason a public boolean operation
failed, read from a [BooleanError](<#BooleanError>) with errors.As. It draws the line the
wrapped sentinel is too coarse to draw: the three codes separate a caller's
three moves (agent-docs/api-design.md §8 / H2).

<a name="BooleanEmpty"></a><a name="BooleanUnsupportedContact"></a><a name="BooleanEvaluatorFailure"></a>

<pre>const (
    // BooleanEmpty is a NORMAL geometric outcome: the operation encloses no
    // volume — a disjoint Intersect, an all-removing Cut. The model is sound and
    // the operation asked for nothing; change the geometry or drop the call. The
    // [BooleanError] wraps [ErrBooleanFailed].
    BooleanEmpty <a href="#BooleanErrorCode">BooleanErrorCode</a> = iota
    // BooleanUnsupportedContact is a VALID model whose boolean geometry reaches a
    // limit: a tessellated curved-surface tangency or near-contact, a coplanar
    // face-on-face overlap, a grazing edge, an isolated-point pinch, or an
    // analytic prism-arrangement refusal wrapping [ErrUnsupported]. The input
    // names a real solid and the refusal is the evaluator&#39;s reach, so the
    // [BooleanError] wraps [ErrUnsupported], never [ErrDegenerate]. Choose a
    // construction that does not lean on that limit, or wait for a later evaluator.
    //
    // A co-directional, coplanar pair of analytic straight prisms takes Union&#39;s
    // analytic reduction and can build. The mesh-path construction this most
    // often costs applies to every other operation and to Union pairs outside
    // that admitted class: two bodies extruded from ONE sketch plane to one end
    // plane whose footprints OVERLAP. Their caps are coplanar by construction and
    // share positive area, which the refusal reads. Coplanar caps on their own
    // are not a contact — two such bodies standing apart in the plane share no cap
    // area, and every boolean over them runs. What replaces the tangent contact is
    // an INTERIOR overlap: no face pair coplanar, and each operand reaching into
    // the other&#39;s interior, so every contact is a transversal crossing this
    // evaluator does classify. Both operands span the same interval here, so a
    // LATERAL displacement never reaches that state — moving one body sideways
    // leaves its caps in the two planes the other&#39;s caps lie in, and the overlap
    // stands wherever the footprints still meet. The displacement has to run
    // ALONG the sweep, and the caller owns what it costs: it changes the enclosed
    // solid, with an effect that depends on the operation and geometry. That
    // displacement is necessary but insufficient when the profiles retain
    // coplanar lateral faces: identical footprints still share lateral face area
    // after their caps separate and return BooleanUnsupportedContact. The caller
    // has to change the profile or otherwise prove that no face pair is coplanar.
    // A displacement leaves a union&#39;s enclosed solid unchanged only when the
    // moved operand is wholly inside the other body both before and after the
    // displacement. Moving an operand into containment removes any former
    // protruding volume.
    BooleanUnsupportedContact
    // BooleanEvaluatorFailure is an internal invariant break: the stitched
    // boundary did not close, a split line was not found, a chain dangled. It is a
    // bug to file. The [BooleanError] wraps [ErrBooleanFailed].
    BooleanEvaluatorFailure
)</pre>

<a name="BooleanOption"></a>
### type BooleanOption

<pre>type BooleanOption interface {
    option.Interface
    // contains filtered or unexported methods
}</pre>

BooleanOption configures Cut and Intersect. An option from another package
cannot implement this sealed tier.

<a name="WithMatchingFaces"></a>
#### func WithMatchingFaces

<pre>func WithMatchingFaces() <a href="#BooleanOption">BooleanOption</a></pre>

WithMatchingFaces tells Cut or Intersect that the operands' faces are meant
to match where they meet: a cap drawn to touch the tool's cone, say, or two
faces meant to coincide. Faces drawn in floating point seldom match exactly;
each rounds on its own, so a design that matches on paper can miss by a few
last-place steps and be refused for it. With this option a miss of that size
is taken as the match the design intends, and its effect is charged into
the result's error bounds. A miss larger than rounding disproves the
declaration, and the operation refuses as it would without the option. The
option never admits a shape that would otherwise be refused for another
reason, and it has no effect on a pair whose faces do not meet.

<a name="BossBore"></a>
### type BossBore

<pre>type BossBore struct {
    Diameter units.Value
    Depth    units.Value
    Head     <a href="#HoleHead">HoleHead</a>
    Thread   *<a href="#HoleThread">HoleThread</a>
    Draft    units.Value
}</pre>

BossBore is the blind pilot hole of a [BossSpec](<#BossSpec>), a round hole drilled down
from the boss's top face. Depth is measured from that top face and is a
positive length. Head is optional and widens the pilot's mouth with a
[Counterbore](<#Counterbore>) or [Countersink](<#Countersink>), as [HoleSpec](<#HoleSpec>).Head does. Thread is optional
and taps the pilot, as [HoleSpec](<#HoleSpec>).Thread does, with Diameter as the tap drill
(agent-docs/boss-design.md §4). Draft is optional and leans the pilot's wall as
[HoleSpec](<#HoleSpec>).Draft does a hole's, narrower toward its bottom for a positive angle;
a pilot that is tapped takes none (ErrDegenerate).

<a name="BossRibs"></a>
### type BossRibs

<pre>type BossRibs struct {
    Count                     <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a>
    Thickness, Length, Height units.Value
    Angle                     units.Value
}</pre>

BossRibs is the set of triangular gusset ribs that brace a [BossSpec](<#BossSpec>)'s root,
spaced evenly round the boss's axis (agent-docs/boss-design.md §9). Each rib
stands Height up the boss's wall and reaches Length out along the face, its
outer edge sloping from the face up to the wall, and is Thickness thick, centred
on the plane through the boss's axis. Count is from 1 to 16, Thickness, Length and
Height are positive lengths with Height at most the boss's Height, and Angle is the
angle of the first rib from the face frame's U axis about the boss's axis: the zero
Value is along U. The ribs are not drawn into the boss's pilot hole.

<a name="BossSpec"></a>
### type BossSpec

<pre>type BossSpec struct {
    Face       <a href="#FaceSelector">FaceSelector</a>
    At         r3.Vec
    Diameter   units.Value
    Height     units.Value
    Bore       *<a href="#BossBore">BossBore</a>
    Draft      units.Value
    RootFillet units.Value
    Shape      <a href="#HoleShape">HoleShape</a>
    // Ribs, when not nil, braces the boss&#39;s root with gusset ribs (agent-docs/boss-design.md §9).
    Ribs *<a href="#BossRibs">BossRibs</a>
    // Tilt, when set, leans the boss&#39;s axis from the face&#39;s normal by this angle, in the
    // direction TiltDirection names (agent-docs/boss-design.md §10). It is an angle above
    // zero and at most 60 degrees, and the zero Value is an upright boss. Height is then
    // measured along the tilted axis from the face. TiltDirection is the angle about the face
    // normal from the face frame&#39;s U axis to the direction the boss leans toward, and its
    // zero Value is along U. A tilted boss is round and takes no Bore, Draft, RootFillet or
    // Ribs, and stands on a planar face.
    Tilt, TiltDirection units.Value
}</pre>

BossSpec describes one boss standing on a planar or cylindrical face: round by
default, or the shape Shape names.

[Face](<#Face>) selects the face the boss stands on and must resolve to exactly one face.
At is a world point in millimetres that lies on that face's plane, or on a
cylindrical face, where the boss stands on the plane tangent there and takes
neither a RootFillet nor a Draft (agent-docs/boss-design.md §8); the boss axis
runs through it, out of the body. Diameter and Height are
positive lengths, Height measured from [Face](<#Face>). Bore is optional, and nil makes
a solid boss. Draft is optional: a positive angle makes the boss narrower
toward its top by that lean of its wall, a negative one wider, and the zero
Value a straight wall (agent-docs/boss-design.md §5). Diameter is the boss's
diameter at [Face](<#Face>) either way. RootFillet is optional: a positive length rounds
the concave edge where the boss meets the face with a fillet of that radius,
and the zero Value leaves the corner sharp (agent-docs/boss-design.md §6).
Shape is optional and replaces the round section with a [RectangularHole](<#RectangularHole>),
[SlotHole](<#SlotHole>) or [PolygonHole](<#PolygonHole>) section, centred on At, as a Hole's shape is: Diameter
is then zero, the shape's size is the boss's size at [Face](<#Face>), and a Draft leans
every wall by its angle (agent-docs/boss-design.md §7). A shaped boss takes no
RootFillet.

<a name="ChainLoftOption"></a>
### type ChainLoftOption

<pre>type ChainLoftOption interface {
    option.Interface
    // contains filtered or unexported methods
}</pre>

ChainLoftOption configures LoftChain. It is its own sealed tier rather than
[LoftOption](<#LoftOption>): WithSurfaceResult() does not implement it, so the compiler
refuses that option outright rather than accepting it as a no-op — a
chain-fed loft always returns a sheet, so there is no cap for the option to
omit (agent-docs/surface-design.md §13.2, agent-docs/loft-design.md §16.3).
WithLoftAlignment is not a member either: Table P's own P4 row forces a
chain pair's offset to 0, so the option would name a correspondence that
does not exist. This placeholder tier has no concrete option yet; it reserves the
call for a later chain-only option.

<a name="ChamferOption"></a>
### type ChamferOption

<pre>type ChamferOption interface {
    // contains filtered or unexported methods
}</pre>

ChamferOption configures Chamfer: WithTangentChain and
WithAsymmetricChamfer (agent-docs/modify-reach-design.md §2).

<a name="WithAsymmetricChamfer"></a>
#### func WithAsymmetricChamfer

<pre>func WithAsymmetricChamfer(reference <a href="#FaceSelector">FaceSelector</a>, otherDistance units.Value) <a href="#ChamferOption">ChamferOption</a></pre>

WithAsymmetricChamfer sets back the chamfer's positional distance across
reference and otherDistance across the other face adjacent to each selected
edge (agent-docs/modify-reach-design.md §6). The option copies reference when it
is called, so a later change to the caller's query does not reach the
chamfer. reference resolves against the receiver after tangent expansion,
and every chamfered edge must have exactly one adjacent face in it, and
every face it resolves to must touch a chamfered edge; anything else is
ErrCardinality. otherDistance is a length magnitude gated like the
positional distance. Passing the option twice is ErrDegenerate.

<a name="Circle3"></a>
### type Circle3

<pre>type Circle3 struct {
    Center r3.Vec
    Axis   r3.Vec
    Radius units.Value
}</pre>

Circle3 is a circular edge. Center is in millimetres, [Axis](<#Axis>) is a unit
normal to its plane, and Radius is the circle radius.

<a name="CircularPattern"></a>
### type CircularPattern

<pre>type CircularPattern struct {
    Center, Axis r3.Vec
    Count        <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a>
}</pre>

CircularPattern places instance i rotated by i/Count of a turn, right-handed
about the axis through Center along [Axis](<#Axis>), i = 0..Count-1. The step angle is
denoted by Count, never by a float, so a quarter turn is exactly a quarter
turn. Center need not lie on the receiver's own sweep axis.

<a name="Clearance"></a>
### type Clearance

<pre>type Clearance = report.<a href="report.md#ClearanceOf">ClearanceOf</a>[*<a href="#Body">Body</a>]</pre>

Clearance is a measured gap between two bodies.

<a name="ClosestPoint"></a>
### type ClosestPoint

<pre>type ClosestPoint struct {
    Point      r3.Vec
    Distance   <a href="#Measurement">Measurement</a>
    OffSurface units.Value
}</pre>

ClosestPoint is the nearest point to a query point that [Body](<#Body>).ClosestPoint and
[Face](<#Face>).ClosestPoint read. Point lies within OffSurface of the true boundary (or
patch), and its distance from the query point is within OffSurface of the
true minimum distance. [Distance](<#Distance>) is the reading DistanceToPoint gives. A
query point inside or on a solid is its own closest point, with OffSurface
zero.

<a name="Container"></a>
### type Container

<pre>type Container struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}</pre>

Container is a named group inside one [Document](<#Document>). It holds sketches, planes and
bodies and nests inside other containers. It is bookkeeping only: it has no
transform, instances nothing and changes no geometry (agent-docs/container-design.md).

A Container belongs to one document for life. Its readers are safe to call
concurrently with Bodies, Remove and Verify; NewChild, ChildNamed, NewUniqueChild,
AddSketch, AddPlane and AddBody mutate the document and are not safe to
run concurrently with another mutation.

<a name="Container.AddBody"></a>
#### func (\*Container) AddBody

<pre>func (c *<a href="#Container">Container</a>) AddBody(b *<a href="#Body">Body</a>) <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a></pre>

AddBody places the live body b in c and takes it out of the container it was
in. Adding b to the container it is already in changes nothing. Nothing else
changes: b keeps its handle, coordinates, provenance and measurements, and no
producer identity advances. A nil c or b is ErrDegenerate, a body of another
document ErrForeignBody, and a retired body ErrRetiredBody.

<a name="Container.AddPlane"></a>
#### func (\*Container) AddPlane

<pre>func (c *<a href="#Container">Container</a>) AddPlane(p *sketch.Plane) <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a></pre>

AddPlane places p in c and takes it out of the container it was in, as
AddSketch does for a sketch.

<a name="Container.AddSketch"></a>
#### func (\*Container) AddSketch

<pre>func (c *<a href="#Container">Container</a>) AddSketch(s *sketch.Sketch) <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a></pre>

AddSketch places s in c and takes it out of the container it was in. Adding it
again to c changes nothing. A sketch never added belongs to the root. A nil s is
ErrDegenerate.

<a name="Container.Bodies"></a>
#### func (\*Container) Bodies

<pre>func (c *<a href="#Container">Container</a>) Bodies() []*<a href="#Body">Body</a></pre>

Bodies lists the live bodies placed directly in c, in creation order. A body
of a child container is not listed. A retired body has left its container.

<a name="Container.ChildNamed"></a>
#### func (\*Container) ChildNamed

<pre>func (c *<a href="#Container">Container</a>) ChildNamed(name <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a>) (*<a href="#Container">Container</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

ChildNamed returns the child of c named name, adding it when c has none. Calls
with one name on one container return the same container. The name is checked as
NewChild checks it (ErrDegenerate).

<a name="Container.Children"></a>
#### func (\*Container) Children

<pre>func (c *<a href="#Container">Container</a>) Children() []*<a href="#Container">Container</a></pre>

Children lists c's child containers in creation order. The slice is a copy.

<a name="Container.Name"></a>
#### func (\*Container) Name

<pre>func (c *<a href="#Container">Container</a>) Name() <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a></pre>

Name returns the container's name; the root's is "".

<a name="Container.NewChild"></a>
#### func (\*Container) NewChild

<pre>func (c *<a href="#Container">Container</a>) NewChild(name <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a>) (*<a href="#Container">Container</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

NewChild adds a container named name under c. The name must be non-empty and
unique among c's children (ErrDegenerate); a container of another document is
ErrForeignBody.

<a name="Container.NewUniqueChild"></a>
#### func (\*Container) NewUniqueChild

<pre>func (c *<a href="#Container">Container</a>) NewUniqueChild(name <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a>) (*<a href="#Container">Container</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

NewUniqueChild adds a container under c named name, or, when a child already has
that name, name followed by " 2", " 3" and so on: the first free one. The name is
checked as NewChild checks it (ErrDegenerate).

<a name="Container.Parent"></a>
#### func (\*Container) Parent

<pre>func (c *<a href="#Container">Container</a>) Parent() *<a href="#Container">Container</a></pre>

Parent returns the container c nests in, or nil for the root.

<pre>func (c *<a href="#Container">Container</a>) Path() <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a></pre>

<a name="ContainerReport"></a>
### type ContainerReport

<pre>type ContainerReport struct {
    // RootBodies are the live bodies placed directly in the root container.
    RootBodies []*<a href="#Body">Body</a>
    // EmptyContainers are the non-root containers with no live body in them or in
    // any container beneath them.

}</pre>

ContainerReport is what VerifyContainers found. Both lists are in a fixed order:
RootBodies in creation order and EmptyContainers in depth-first order of the tree,
children in creation order.

<a name="ContainerReport.Err"></a>
#### func (\*ContainerReport) Err

<pre>func (r *<a href="#ContainerReport">ContainerReport</a>) Err() <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a></pre>

Err returns nil when Passed, and otherwise an error wrapping ErrContainerLayout.
It names each root body by its 1-based place among the live bodies and each empty
container by its path.

<a name="ContainerReport.Passed"></a>
#### func (\*ContainerReport) Passed

<pre>func (r *<a href="#ContainerReport">ContainerReport</a>) Passed() <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#bool">bool</a></pre>

Passed reports whether the layout is clean: no body in the root and no empty
container.

<a name="CopyOption"></a>
### type CopyOption

<pre>type CopyOption interface {
    option.Interface
    // contains filtered or unexported methods
}</pre>

CopyOption configures Copy. Only WithCopyPlacement, WithCopyRotation and
WithCopyLiftTranslation change the copy's placement. An option from another package cannot implement
this sealed tier.

<a name="WithCopyLiftTranslation"></a>
#### func WithCopyLiftTranslation

<pre>func WithCopyLiftTranslation(lift r3.Transform, from, to r3.Vec) <a href="#CopyOption">CopyOption</a></pre>

WithCopyLiftTranslation places a new copy by moving the point from to the
point to, both given in lift's local coordinates. The exact world translation
is the lift's linear part times to minus from, formed in exact rationals: the
subtraction and the product round nothing. A faceted copy denotes its
source's true solid moved by exactly that vector, and its held vertices are
charged for the rounding of the held placement to the nearest float
translation. Other payloads are placed by that float translation alone,
exactly as WithCopyPlacement of it.

The copy is marked as exactly placed like every exact copy, so VerifyMotion
and VerifyLinkage refuse to re-place it. Only a copy made directly from its
source records the translation: Transform and a copy of a copy record none.
Verify reads a direct copy as its source moved by the exact vector, so a
copy that stays inside a body the lift-local source stayed inside (a pin
moved from one bore sketched on the lift to another) is decided from the
recorded history.

An invalid lift is ErrDegenerate and a non-finite from or to is
ErrNotFinite, both when Copy evaluates the option. A to that equals from is the
identity.

<a name="WithCopyPlacement"></a>
#### func WithCopyPlacement

<pre>func WithCopyPlacement(t r3.Transform) <a href="#CopyOption">CopyOption</a></pre>

WithCopyPlacement places a new copy under t. A zero or otherwise invalid
transform is ErrDegenerate when Copy evaluates the option.

<a name="WithCopyRotation"></a>
#### func WithCopyRotation

<pre>func WithCopyRotation(center, axis r3.Vec, angle units.Value) <a href="#CopyOption">CopyOption</a></pre>

WithCopyRotation places a new copy by a rotation about the axis through
center along axis, by angle. The rotation a faceted copy denotes is an
exactly orthogonal rational rotation about exactly that axis, chosen near
angle: it agrees with angle to within a few float steps, but it is not in
general the rotation by exactly that transcendental angle. The held
placement's rounding is charged against that exact rotation. Other payloads
are placed by r3.RotationAround(center, axis, angle), exactly as
WithCopyPlacement of that transform.

A faceted copy made this way keeps the analytic tag of a face that a mesh
Boolean retained from its operands (a plane, cylinder, sphere or torus), with
a NormalAt bound that charges the float image of the tag against the exact
rotation; a retained cone keeps the bound 2. Every other face reads as
[Faceted](<#Faceted>) with its held bound, so [Face](<#Face>).NormalAt refuses it and [ToFace](<#ToFace>) stops
refuse it. A rotated plane tag is a float image, so [MirrorFace](<#MirrorFace>) refuses it.
The copy also stops being a point-loft source. Use WithCopyPlacement for a
copy that needs those readings.

A zero or non-finite axis is ErrDegenerate, a non-finite center or angle is
ErrNotFinite, and an angle that is not an angle is ErrUnitKind, all when
Copy evaluates the option. A zero angle is the identity.

<a name="Counterbore"></a>
### type Counterbore

<pre>type Counterbore struct {
    Diameter units.Value
    Depth    units.Value
}</pre>

Counterbore cuts a flat-bottomed cylindrical recess Depth deep and Diameter
wide at the mouth. Diameter is a length wider than the hole, and Depth is a
length shorter than the hole.

<a name="Countersink"></a>
### type Countersink

<pre>type Countersink struct {
    Diameter units.Value
    Angle    units.Value
}</pre>

Countersink cuts a conical recess Diameter wide at the face. Angle is the
included angle of the cone, strictly between 0 and 180 degrees; 90 degrees
is the common metric flat-head screw. Diameter is a length wider than the
hole, and the cone's depth is set by Diameter, Angle and the hole diameter.

<a name="Document"></a>
### type Document

<pre>type Document struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}</pre>

Document is the mutable root of a model: it owns the live body set and the
producer identities used for topology provenance. It is immediate-mode —
the caller's Go function is the feature tree (core §6) — and it is NOT
safe for concurrent mutation (core §12), with one guarded exception: the
live body set sits behind its node's LiveMu, so Bodies, Remove and Verify may run
concurrently with one another. The bodies it hands out are immutable and
safe to read from anywhere.

<a name="New"></a>
#### func New

<pre>func New(opts ...<a href="#DocumentOption">DocumentOption</a>) *<a href="#Document">Document</a></pre>

New returns an empty document.

<a name="Document.Bindings"></a>
#### func (\*Document) Bindings

<pre>func (d *<a href="#Document">Document</a>) Bindings() []<a href="#Binding">Binding</a></pre>

Bindings returns every Param and Expr read the document has made, in call
order. The slice is a copy.

<a name="Document.Bodies"></a>
#### func (\*Document) Bodies

<pre>func (d *<a href="#Document">Document</a>) Bodies() []*<a href="#Body">Body</a></pre>

Bodies returns the live bodies — the model as it stands. The slice is a
copy; the elements are the live (immutable) bodies.

<a name="Document.ContactPair"></a>
#### func (\*Document) ContactPair

<pre>func (d *<a href="#Document">Document</a>) ContactPair(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, a, b *<a href="#Body">Body</a>, poseA, poseB r3.Transform,
    req <a href="#ContactRequest">ContactRequest</a>) (*<a href="#ContactReport">ContactReport</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

ContactPair proves the relation of two live solids at poses applied after
their recorded placements. Bodies and the document are not changed.
Source rectangular prisms have face manifolds at signed-axis poses and
co-oriented oblique face touches. Opposed axis-normal oriented faces can
publish a common interior witness. Other valid poses have relation proofs.
Source semicircle spheres against boxes or each other also have relation
and point-manifold proofs at signed-axis poses, or at proper rotating poses
when the sphere center is the query origin. [Sphere](<#Sphere>)-pair center lines
may be off-axis when their normal and witnesses meet the requested bounds.
A full source cylinder, extruded or revolved, can prove an axial gap and
disk-face contact against a containing box face. A vertical full circular
source prism can also prove a horizontal sidewall gap and line contact.
A faceted solid with an exact lower support certificate can prove lower
support face contact or an axial gap
against a source-box floor that strictly contains its support footprint.
An exact source box's lower face survives a positive-bound Union when the
other operand's certified lower bound is strictly above it. Other
positive-bound faceted solids can prove a strict axial gap with their
boundary displacement charged, but publish no contact manifold.
An exactly orthogonal rotated source box can give a sphere a bounded point
on one interior face.
Two exact planar solids — prisms over whole LineSeg sections and
zero-bound faceted Booleans — receive an exact relation proof at any pose
with a positive determinant. When one is convex, a touch publishes its
clipped face patches, edges and vertices inside a face, and edge
crossings, and two convex bodies that overlap slightly publish the patch
at depth. When neither body is convex, a touch whose every contact lies
on one flat face of one body, the other body wholly on or in front of its
plane, publishes the other body's corners strictly inside that face with
its normal; any other touching or overlapping pair names
ContactNonConvex. A positive-bound faceted Boolean, a displaced
stitched solid, and every other solid without an exact contact family of
its own (a cap-loop chamfer, a cup, a loft, a sweep, a general revolve) are
admitted through their held meshes with the mesh's boundary displacement δ
charged: an all-planar body is read at a chord that chords nothing, and a
body with a curved face at the request's HeldChord, which must be positive.
A held touch, or a held gap or depth within the summed δ, is ContactBand
with Gap \[−2δ, 2δ\]. Under a positive
SupportBand an exact planar touch or shallow face overlap also publishes the
support set: every vertex of the resting body within the band above a face
plane of the other, its foot strictly inside that face, at its exact
height; and an exact planar pair apart by at most the band is ContactBand
with Gap \[0 ± g\], g its gap's upper end, publishing that set
(agent-docs/multibody-dynamics-design.md §10.5).
At identity query poses, the analytic clearance kernel can prove relations
for other solids. Only its ruling touches publish a manifold: the two ends
of a full source cylinder's ruling on a planar face or another cylinder.
At other poses a full source cylinder lying along a signed-axis face of an
exact planar body proves a touch or gap at a signed-axis pose, and at any
other pose a gap, or a ContactBand whose width charges the pose basis's
rounding, each with the two lowest rim points as its manifold.
Both bodies must be non-nil, distinct, live members of d.

<a name="Document.Expr"></a>
#### func (\*Document) Expr

<pre>func (d *<a href="#Document">Document</a>) Expr(expr <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a>) (units.Value, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

Expr evaluates an ad-hoc expression against the parameter table and returns
it in the base unit of the kind it computes to (millimetre for a length,
radian for an angle). An expression mixing kinds incompatibly is
param.ErrIncompatibleKind. The read is recorded in Bindings.

<a name="Document.OperationHistory"></a>
#### func (\*Document) OperationHistory

<pre>func (d *<a href="#Document">Document</a>) OperationHistory() *<a href="#OperationHistory">OperationHistory</a></pre>

[OperationHistory](<#OperationHistory>) returns an immutable snapshot of all recorded calls.

<a name="Document.Param"></a>
#### func (\*Document) Param

<pre>func (d *<a href="#Document">Document</a>) Param(name <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a>) (units.Value, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

Param evaluates the named parameter and returns it in its declared unit, so
the result passes anywhere a feature takes a [units.Value](<https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/lestrrat-3d/units#Value>), such as an
extent distance, a fillet radius or a chamfer distance. An undefined name or
a cycle is the table's own error (param.ErrUndefined, param.ErrCycle). The
read is recorded in Bindings.

<a name="Document.ParamInt"></a>
#### func (\*Document) ParamInt

<pre>func (d *<a href="#Document">Document</a>) ParamInt(name <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a>) (<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

ParamInt evaluates the named dimensionless parameter as a whole number, for
an argument such as a pattern Count. A value that is not an integer, or a
parameter that carries a unit, is ErrDegenerate.

<a name="Document.Params"></a>
#### func (\*Document) Params

<pre>func (d *<a href="#Document">Document</a>) Params() *param.Table</pre>

Params returns the document's parameter table. Define parameters on it with
Set, SetExpr or SetValue, then read them with Param and Expr. Changing the
table and running the builder again is how a model is edited.

<a name="Document.Root"></a>
#### func (\*Document) Root

<pre>func (d *<a href="#Document">Document</a>) Root() *<a href="#Container">Container</a></pre>

Root returns the document's root container, named "". A body, sketch or plane
never placed elsewhere belongs to it.

<a name="Document.SweepPair"></a>
#### func (\*Document) SweepPair

<pre>func (d *<a href="#Document">Document</a>) SweepPair(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, a, b *<a href="#Body">Body</a>, pathA, pathB <a href="#PairPath">PairPath</a>,
    req <a href="#SweepRequest">SweepRequest</a>) (*<a href="#SweepReport">SweepReport</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

SweepPair certifies the first encounter of two live solids under one shared
duration. Continuous proofs cover affine source-box paths, exact faceted
floor contact and bounded faceted floor clearance, co-translating oblique
source boxes, a source sphere in
an axis or orthogonal rotated box face corridor, an affine pair of source
spheres, source-cylinder face paths, rotating source-box and centered-sphere rigid drifts,
and admitted rotating PoseSegments. Two exact planar solids — prisms over
whole LineSeg sections and zero-bound faceted Booleans — that no narrower
path admits receive a clear path or a first-impact bracket under any rotating
or affine path, and from an initial touch a departure or a persistent touch
or band track (agent-docs/multibody-dynamics-design.md §10.2, §10.3). A
positive-bound faceted Boolean or all-planar cap-loop chamfer takes the
same run through its held mesh under §10.4: a first impact brackets onto a
ContactBand sample, and a band start never departs but may carry a band
track widened by twice the displacement. Under a positive SupportBand the
band track runs over §10.5's support set and ends before any of its
vertices reaches the plane, and an exact pair that starts inside the band
may depart. A full source cylinder whose
ruling touches a face of an exact planar body that only translates may,
under a spinning drift, carry §10.4's rolling touch or band track.
Unsupported paths return SweepUndecided.
Both body pointers, both paths, and ctx must be non-nil.

<a name="Document.SweptBox"></a>
#### func (\*Document) SweptBox

<pre>func (d *<a href="#Document">Document</a>) SweptBox(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, b *<a href="#Body">Body</a>, path <a href="#PairPath">PairPath</a>) (<a href="#SweptBox">SweptBox</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

[SweptBox](<#SweptBox>) returns the box b sweeps along path. It validates b and path as
SweepPair does, and returns ErrUnsupported when b's bounds or the path's
travel bound are not finite. It changes neither b nor the document.
b, path and ctx must be non-nil.

<a name="Document.Verify"></a>
#### func (\*Document) Verify

<pre>func (d *<a href="#Document">Document</a>) Verify(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, opts ...<a href="#VerifyOption">VerifyOption</a>) (*<a href="#Report">Report</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

Verify is one non-mutating call over the live model: solidity and boundary
validity per body, every quantity judged by the tolerance gate, and the
pairwise partition — proven overlap, proven disjointness, or Suspect
(verification §1/§6). It mirrors sketch.Verify (core §10).

Verify checks interference even when no options are passed. For each pair of
proven-valid bodies that cheaper proofs do not settle, its mesh fallback
checks every pair of operand facet boxes before pruning exact predicates. A
pair holding a sheet operand never reaches that fallback: it is decided by
box separation, or, when the boxes meet, the sheet decision procedure of
agent-docs/surface-design.md §9.3. One pair's
work can therefore grow with the two facet counts multiplied together, and
total work also grows with the number of unresolved body pairs. Verify
proves those pairs on up to GOMAXPROCS goroutines (at most 12) and builds
the report in pair order, so the report and any returned error match a
one-pair-at-a-time walk (agent-docs/interference-design.md §2). Large-model
callers should pass a context with a deadline chosen from representative
inputs. For a document with live bodies, after document and option
validation, cancellation returns ctx.Err() and a nil report; validation
errors take precedence even when ctx is already canceled. An empty document
retains its Sound result even when the context is already canceled. The
document remains unchanged. Verify reads the live set once, as it stands
when the call begins, so a concurrent Remove never changes the bodies one
call reports on.

<a name="Document.VerifyContainers"></a>
#### func (\*Document) VerifyContainers

<pre>func (d *<a href="#Document">Document</a>) VerifyContainers() *<a href="#ContainerReport">ContainerReport</a></pre>

VerifyContainers checks the document's container layout without touching
geometry: every live body should sit in a named container, and every non-root
container should hold a body, directly or in a container beneath it. A document
that never uses a container reports every body as a root body.

<a name="Document.VerifyJointBox"></a>
#### func (\*Document) VerifyJointBox

<pre>func (d *<a href="#Document">Document</a>) VerifyJointBox(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, l *<a href="#Linkage">Linkage</a>, box <a href="#JointBox">JointBox</a>, opts ...<a href="#JointBoxOption">JointBoxOption</a>) (*<a href="#JointBoxReport">JointBoxReport</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

VerifyJointBox checks whether every configuration in box is clear: whether
no link of l, at any joint values the box holds, meets a static body or a
body of another link (agent-docs/linkage-check-design.md §14). It never changes
the document: each centre re-evaluates every link body's payload under its
link's pose as a transient body that is never committed.

The box is cut into cells. A cell is CellClear only when every pair's
proven gap at the cell's centre exceeds τ\_half, the chain travel bound of
§5.2 over half the cell's weighted span, so no configuration of the cell
can close it; a cell its centre neither certifies nor proves colliding is
halved along the joint that most lowers τ\_half for the pair that held it
back, shallowest cells first, until the resolution — a Dimensionless
fraction of each varying joint's own range — or WithCellBudget stops it. A
cell left uncertified reads CellUndecided and makes the report Suspect,
never Sound.

A closed loop ([Linkage](<#Linkage>).Close) is varied at its driver alone: the box lists
at most one joint of each loop, whose parent is the loop's common link, and
every other joint of the loop follows it (agent-docs/linkage-check-design.md
§16). Each cell reads the loop's dependent joints from sketch's certified
enclosures, as VerifyLinkage reads a drive's intervals: their enclosure at
the centre is charged into the pose deviation, and the distance from it to
the far end of their hull over the cell into τ\_half. A cell sketch cannot
enclose is never CellClear or CellBlocked.

The options are VerifyLinkage's (WithMotionTolerance, WithResolution,
WithMinClearance) plus WithCellBudget. Every body of every link, and every
body a declared joint contact names, MUST be a live body of d. A nil
context, document or linkage, a linkage with no link, a box with no varying
joint, a range with Min \> Max, a link named twice, two joints of one loop,
a range end outside a joint's declared limits, a dependent joint whose
certified hull is not proven inside its limits, and a budget below 1 are
decaderr.ErrDegenerate; a loop joint whose parent is not the loop's common link, and
a loop whose zero pose sketch cannot enclose, are decaderr.ErrUnsupported.
Validation precedes cancellation; after it a canceled context returns
ctx.Err() and no report.

<a name="Document.VerifyLinkage"></a>
#### func (\*Document) VerifyLinkage

<pre>func (d *<a href="#Document">Document</a>) VerifyLinkage(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, l *<a href="#Linkage">Linkage</a>, drive <a href="#Drive">Drive</a>, opts ...<a href="#MotionOption">MotionOption</a>) (*<a href="#LinkageReport">LinkageReport</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

VerifyLinkage checks whether any link of l, moved along drive, meets a
static body or a body of another link anywhere on the drive
(agent-docs/linkage-check-design.md). It never changes the document: each pose
re-evaluates every link body's payload under its link's pose as a
transient body that is never committed, so [Document](<#Document>).Bodies(), every body's
live state and the next producer identity are what they were before the
call.

The options are VerifyMotion's own (WithMotionTolerance, WithResolution,
WithMinClearance), with the resolution a Dimensionless fraction of the
drive, default units.Scalar(1.0/1024). Every pair result at a pose is
Verify's own row or diagnostic. [Between](<#Between>) two adjacent poses the interval
certificate proves the drive clear only when every pair's two proven lower
bounds together exceed the chain travel bound τ (§5.2), summed over the
joints below the pair's lowest common ancestor, each joint's travel taken on
both sides of every waypoint inside the interval; an interval it cannot
certify down to the resolution is IntervalUndecided and the report reads
Suspect, never Sound. A pose publishes a [LinkCollision](<#LinkCollision>) only for an overlap
that survives the pose's own deviation from the ideal poses (§5.1).

Declared joint contacts ([Linkage](<#Linkage>).DeclareJointContact) are checked for
proven overlap at every pose but enter no interval certificate; the report
lists them in JointContacts.

Every body of every link, and every body a declared joint contact names,
MUST be a live body of d. A nil context, document or linkage, a linkage
with no link, a drive in which every sweep holds, a drive whose sweeps carry
different numbers of Via values, and a drive with a waypoint outside a
joint's declared limits are decaderr.ErrDegenerate. Validation precedes
cancellation; after it a canceled context returns ctx.Err() and no report.

<a name="Document.VerifyMotion"></a>
#### func (\*Document) VerifyMotion

<pre>func (d *<a href="#Document">Document</a>) VerifyMotion(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, moving []*<a href="#Body">Body</a>, m <a href="#Motion">Motion</a>, opts ...<a href="#MotionOption">MotionOption</a>) (*<a href="#MotionReport">MotionReport</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

VerifyMotion checks whether the rigid set moving, carried along m, meets
any other live body of d anywhere on the path (agent-docs/motion-check-design.md).
It never changes the document: each pose re-evaluates a mover's payload
under the composed motion as a transient body that is never committed, so
[Document](<#Document>).Bodies(), every body's live state and the next producer identity
are what they were before the call.

Every pair result at a pose is Verify's own row or diagnostic. [Between](<#Between>) two
adjacent poses the interval certificate (§5.2) proves the path clear only
when every (mover, static) pair's two proven lower bounds together exceed
the farthest any mover point can travel across the interval; an interval it
cannot certify down to the resolution is IntervalUndecided and the report
reads Suspect, never Sound. A pose publishes a [Collision](<#Collision>) only for an overlap
that survives the pose's own deviation from the ideal motion (§5.1).

moving MUST be non-empty, hold live bodies of d, and list no body twice.
A nil context returns ErrDegenerate before validation. Other validation
errors precede cancellation; after validation a canceled context returns
ctx.Err() and no report.

<a name="DocumentOption"></a>
### type DocumentOption

<pre>type DocumentOption interface {
    option.Interface
    // contains filtered or unexported methods
}</pre>

DocumentOption configures New. WithGapTolerance, ExactOnly,
WithChainTolerance and WithParams are its options. An option from another package cannot implement this sealed tier.

<a name="ExactOnly"></a>
#### func ExactOnly

<pre>func ExactOnly() <a href="#DocumentOption">DocumentOption</a></pre>

ExactOnly keeps every result exact: the evaluator never moves a held vertex
off the exact point it stands for beyond the float rounding that point
needs, and refuses a result that only such a move would keep embedded.

<a name="WithChainTolerance"></a>
#### func WithChainTolerance

<pre>func WithChainTolerance(tol units.Value) <a href="#DocumentOption">DocumentOption</a></pre>

WithChainTolerance sets the coarsest bound a held facet may carry where a
boolean's two operands meet. The default is the pair's own chord tolerance,
so a Cut, Union or Intersect whose contact touches facets that an earlier
boolean left coarser than that is refused with a message naming the facet's
bound and the tolerance. A document that sets this admits a contact whose
touched facets are within tol. Every bound the result carries is still
proven; a larger tol lets a chain of booleans over curved solids reach a
larger bound, and the result reads Approximate with a Bound that covers it.
A value that is not a length is ErrUnitKind, a non-finite one ErrNotFinite
and a negative one ErrNegativeMagnitude, all when an operation that reads
it starts. A zero length is the default.

<a name="WithGapTolerance"></a>
#### func WithGapTolerance

<pre>func WithGapTolerance(tol units.Value) <a href="#DocumentOption">DocumentOption</a></pre>

WithGapTolerance sets the farthest the evaluator may move a held vertex from
the exact point it stands for to keep a result embedded. A result the exact
rounding would fold through itself, and so refuse, is kept when moving the
offending vertices by up to tol clears it; the move is charged to that
vertex's bound, so the result reads Approximate with a Bound that covers it
(agent-docs/gap-tolerance-design.md). A document with no option uses
0\.01 mm. A value that is not a length is ErrUnitKind, a non-finite one
ErrNotFinite and a negative one ErrNegativeMagnitude, all when an operation
that reads it starts. A zero length is ExactOnly.

<a name="WithParams"></a>
#### func WithParams

<pre>func WithParams(t *param.Table) <a href="#DocumentOption">DocumentOption</a></pre>

WithParams makes the document read its parameters from t, such as the table
a sketch World returns from Params, so a sketch dimension and a feature
value derive from the same definitions. The document does not copy t: a
later Set on it changes what the next read returns. A nil t is ignored. A
document with no option owns a fresh table.

<a name="DraftOption"></a>
### type DraftOption

<pre>type DraftOption interface {
    option.Interface
    // contains filtered or unexported methods
}</pre>

DraftOption is a placeholder option tier for [Draft](<#Draft>). It carries no
option today and reserves the signature for a later draft option.

<a name="Drive"></a>
### type Drive

<pre>type Drive = linkage.<a href="linkage.md#Drive">Drive</a>[*<a href="#Body">Body</a>]</pre>

Drive is a one-parameter motion of a linkage.

<a name="Edge"></a>
### type Edge

<pre>type Edge struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}</pre>

Edge is a topological edge: a tagged curve between two vertices, with the
faces adjacent to it.

<a name="Edge.Curve"></a>
#### func (\*Edge) Curve

<pre>func (e *<a href="#Edge">Edge</a>) Curve() <a href="#Curve">Curve</a></pre>

[Curve](<#Curve>) returns the edge's tagged geometry.

<a name="Edge.End"></a>
#### func (\*Edge) End

<pre>func (e *<a href="#Edge">Edge</a>) End() *<a href="#Vertex">Vertex</a></pre>

End returns the edge's end vertex.

<a name="Edge.Faces"></a>
#### func (\*Edge) Faces

<pre>func (e *<a href="#Edge">Edge</a>) Faces() []*<a href="#Face">Face</a></pre>

Faces returns the faces adjacent to this edge. What len(Faces()) means is
read per body kind (agent-docs/surface-design.md §2.2, core §6.1): on a
BodySolid, one adjacent face is non-manifold; on a BodySheet, one adjacent
face is a FREE edge — the boundary of the sheet, and the expected shape —
which IsFree reports and the Free() predicate selects. Two is an interior
edge on either kind; three or more is non-manifold on either.

<a name="Edge.IsConvex"></a>
#### func (\*Edge) IsConvex

<pre>func (e *<a href="#Edge">Edge</a>) IsConvex() <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#bool">bool</a></pre>

IsConvex reports the edge's convexity under decad's WALKED-BOUNDARY
convention — a decided answer, not an approximation of one (core §6). It is
the sense of the 2D profile walk that produced the edge, NOT the 3D material
angle across it; the two agree where two walls meet and part company at a
rim.

Every profile is walked with the material on the left: the outer loop
counter-clockwise, every hole clockwise (internal/momentregion). Three classes of edge
read that walk:

- A JUNCTION edge, where two walls meet, is convex when the walk turns
  left there — the material wedge closes to less than a half turn — and
  concave when it turns right. This one is also the material angle.
- A RIM edge, a wall's own copy in a cap plane, takes the sense of the
  wall it runs along: a CIRCULAR wall by its own turn — walked
  counter-clockwise convex, clockwise concave — and a STRAIGHT wall, which
  turns not at all, by the role of the loop it belongs to: outer convex,
  hole concave.
- The on-axis edge shared by both caps of a partial revolve is convex when
  the sweep is less than a half turn: there the two caps ARE the adjacent
  faces, and the sweep is the angle between them.

So a HOLE's rim edges are CONCAVE, and so are the rim edges of a concave
round bitten out of the outer boundary — even though the material across
such a rim is a plain quarter-turn wedge a chamfer could take. Convexity
here is the walk's answer, not the wedge's: Concave() picks a hole's rim,
Convex() never does.

<a name="Edge.IsFree"></a>
#### func (\*Edge) IsFree

<pre>func (e *<a href="#Edge">Edge</a>) IsFree() <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#bool">bool</a></pre>

IsFree reports whether exactly one face is adjacent to this edge — a
sheet's boundary, and the expected shape there (agent-docs/surface-design.md
§2.2). On a BodySolid the same count of one is non-manifold rather than
free; IsFree only names the count Faces reports, and Faces's own doc comment
states the per-kind reading in full.

<a name="Edge.Length"></a>
#### func (\*Edge) Length

<pre>func (e *<a href="#Edge">Edge</a>) Length() (<a href="#Measurement">Measurement</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

Length returns the edge's length: Exact only when the analytic result is
proved exactly representable, otherwise Approximate with its evaluation
bound. A boolean-built straight rim (two planar sources) carries its proven
chord bound. A boolean rim on a curved source has a true length the chord
chain provably understates by an amount this evaluator cannot bound, so it
is ErrUnsupported — an honest refusal, never an understated Bound. A
cap-loop chamfer's miter ruling is the same refusal one construction over:
where either carrier meeting at the corner is circular, the ruling's tagged
chord understates the curved locus the exact offset family denotes
(agent-docs/modify-reach-design.md §8.3), and a corner whose locus enclosure this
evaluator cannot build refuses the same way rather than publish an
understated Bound.

<a name="Edge.Start"></a>
#### func (\*Edge) Start

<pre>func (e *<a href="#Edge">Edge</a>) Start() *<a href="#Vertex">Vertex</a></pre>

Start returns the edge's start vertex.

<a name="Edge.Wedge"></a>
#### func (\*Edge) Wedge

<pre>func (e *<a href="#Edge">Edge</a>) Wedge() <a href="#EdgeWedge">EdgeWedge</a></pre>

Wedge reads the MATERIAL wedge across the edge: whether the solid's material
angle there is reflex or salient. It is not IsConvex, which reads the
walked boundary: a boss root on a Union result is IsConvex but
WedgeReflex, and a hole's rim is concave by IsConvex but WedgeSalient.

It answers only where the two faces' outward normals ([Face](<#Face>).NormalAt) decide
the sign of their turn beyond their proven bounds at every end of the edge,
and only for an edge whose angle cannot change along it: a line between two
planes, a line between a plane and a cylinder parallel to it, and a circle
or arc on a plane normal to its axis meeting a coaxial cylinder, cone,
sphere or torus. Every other edge is WedgeUndecided: a tangent junction, an
edge of a [Faceted](<#Faceted>) face, a [FacetedCurve](<#FacetedCurve>) edge, a line between two cylinders,
and a free or non-manifold edge.

<a name="EdgeAxis"></a>
### type EdgeAxis

<pre>type EdgeAxis struct {
    Body *<a href="#Body">Body</a>
    Edge <a href="#EdgeSelector">EdgeSelector</a>
}</pre>

EdgeAxis is a linear edge, selected — never a pointer. [Body](<#Body>) is what [Edge](<#Edge>)
resolves against: a Revolve is handed no body, so the axis must name its
own. [Edge](<#Edge>) MUST resolve to exactly one linear edge of [Body](<#Body>) — any other
count is ErrCardinality, zero included (the implicit exactly-one of
core §12), and a non-linear edge named as an axis is ErrDegenerate. [Body](<#Body>)
must be a live body of the same document at the call and is not consumed or
retired. The axis
runs from the resolved edge's start vertex toward its end vertex, the
sense Along is right-handed about.

<a name="EdgePredicate"></a>
### type EdgePredicate

<pre>type EdgePredicate struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}</pre>

EdgePredicate is one clause of an [EdgeQuery](<#EdgeQuery>). Predicates come
only from the package constructors — Convex, Concave, Reflex, Salient,
ParallelTo, EndpointAt, LongerThan, CreatedBy, Circular, Free — and compose by
conjunction within a branch ([EdgeQuery](<#EdgeQuery>).Or adds a branch); the zero
value names no predicate and is rejected at resolve.

<a name="Circular"></a>
#### func Circular

<pre>func Circular() <a href="#EdgePredicate">EdgePredicate</a></pre>

Circular matches edges whose curve is a full circle or a circular arc.

<a name="Concave"></a>
#### func Concave

<pre>func Concave() <a href="#EdgePredicate">EdgePredicate</a></pre>

Concave matches edges [Edge](<#Edge>).IsConvex reports concave — the walked-boundary
convention, not the 3D material angle across the edge. This is the predicate
that picks a hole's rim edges, and the rim of a concave round bitten out of
the outer boundary.

<a name="Convex"></a>
#### func Convex

<pre>func Convex() <a href="#EdgePredicate">EdgePredicate</a></pre>

Convex matches edges [Edge](<#Edge>).IsConvex reports convex — the walked-boundary
convention, not the 3D material angle across the edge. Read [Edge](<#Edge>).IsConvex
before selecting on it: a hole's rim edges are CONCAVE, so this predicate
never picks them.

<a name="CreatedBy"></a>
#### func CreatedBy

<pre>func CreatedBy(f <a href="#FeatureRef">FeatureRef</a>) <a href="#EdgePredicate">EdgePredicate</a></pre>

CreatedBy matches edges by provenance: edges created by the feature role f
names. Provenance is structural, so it survives body rebuilds
(agent-docs/evaluator-design.md §3). A negative producer identity or empty role is rejected at
resolve as ErrDegenerate.

<a name="EndpointAt"></a>
#### func EndpointAt

<pre>func EndpointAt(p r3.Vec) <a href="#EdgePredicate">EdgePredicate</a></pre>

EndpointAt matches an edge whose stored start or end position equals p
component-wise. It uses no tolerance; a non-finite p fails at resolve.

<a name="Free"></a>
#### func Free

<pre>func Free() <a href="#EdgePredicate">EdgePredicate</a></pre>

Free matches edges [Edge](<#Edge>).IsFree reports free — exactly one adjacent face, a
sheet's boundary (agent-docs/surface-design.md §2.2, §3.1). It composes with
every other clause: Edges(Free(), Circular()) picks the circular free
edges, Edges(Free()).Exactly(8) asserts a surface extrude's rim count. On a
body with no free edge — every solid, and a closed sheet — it matches
nothing, an ordinary ErrNoMatch at resolve or ErrCardinality under an
assertion, never an error in itself.

<a name="LongerThan"></a>
#### func LongerThan

<pre>func LongerThan(l units.Value) <a href="#EdgePredicate">EdgePredicate</a></pre>

LongerThan matches edges strictly longer than l. The quantity is recorded
exactly as given; a non-length or negative l is rejected at resolve
(ErrUnitKind / ErrNegativeMagnitude), not here.

<a name="OuterLoopOf"></a>
#### func OuterLoopOf

<pre>func OuterLoopOf(f <a href="#FeatureRef">FeatureRef</a>) <a href="#EdgePredicate">EdgePredicate</a></pre>

OuterLoopOf matches edges on the outer boundary loop of a face carrying f.
On a holed cap, it excludes every inner-loop rim edge, including a bore.

<a name="ParallelTo"></a>
#### func ParallelTo

<pre>func ParallelTo(v r3.Vec) <a href="#EdgePredicate">EdgePredicate</a></pre>

ParallelTo matches edges whose direction is parallel to v. The vector is
recorded exactly as given — a dimensionless direction (core §5.2); a
degenerate (zero or non-finite) direction is rejected at resolve, not here.

<a name="Reflex"></a>
#### func Reflex

<pre>func Reflex() <a href="#EdgePredicate">EdgePredicate</a></pre>

Reflex matches edges [Edge](<#Edge>).Wedge reads WedgeReflex: the material angle across
the edge is over a half turn, as at a boss root or an inside corner. It is
the predicate that picks the root of a boss on a Union result, which
Concave does not. An edge whose wedge is WedgeUndecided matches neither
Reflex nor Salient.

<a name="Salient"></a>
#### func Salient

<pre>func Salient() <a href="#EdgePredicate">EdgePredicate</a></pre>

Salient matches edges [Edge](<#Edge>).Wedge reads WedgeSalient: the material angle
across the edge is under a half turn, as at a box's outer edge or a hole's
rim. An edge whose wedge is WedgeUndecided matches neither Salient nor
Reflex.

<a name="EdgeQuery"></a>
### type EdgeQuery

<pre>type EdgeQuery struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}</pre>

EdgeQuery is the concrete edge selector: a union of branches, each a
conjunction of edge predicates, plus an optional cardinality assertion over
the union. Build one with Edges and add branches with Or.

<a name="Edges"></a>
#### func Edges

<pre>func Edges(preds ...<a href="#EdgePredicate">EdgePredicate</a>) *<a href="#EdgeQuery">EdgeQuery</a></pre>

Edges returns a query matching every edge that satisfies all of preds; no
predicates matches every edge. A query that matches nothing at resolve is
an error, loudly — ErrNoMatch, or ErrCardinality when asserted (core §9).

<a name="EdgeQuery.AtLeast"></a>
#### func (\*EdgeQuery) AtLeast

<pre>func (q *<a href="#EdgeQuery">EdgeQuery</a>) AtLeast(n <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a>) *<a href="#EdgeQuery">EdgeQuery</a></pre>

AtLeast asserts the query resolves to at least n matches; fewer is
ErrCardinality at resolve. It replaces any earlier cardinality assertion
and returns the receiver for chaining.

<a name="EdgeQuery.Exactly"></a>
#### func (\*EdgeQuery) Exactly

<pre>func (q *<a href="#EdgeQuery">EdgeQuery</a>) Exactly(n <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a>) *<a href="#EdgeQuery">EdgeQuery</a></pre>

Exactly asserts the query resolves to exactly n matches; anything else —
zero included — is ErrCardinality at resolve. It replaces any earlier
cardinality assertion and returns the receiver for chaining.

<a name="EdgeQuery.Or"></a>
#### func (\*EdgeQuery) Or

<pre>func (q *<a href="#EdgeQuery">EdgeQuery</a>) Or(preds ...<a href="#EdgePredicate">EdgePredicate</a>) *<a href="#EdgeQuery">EdgeQuery</a></pre>

Or adds a union branch: the query then also matches every edge that
satisfies all of preds. An edge that several branches match is selected
once, in [Body](<#Body>).Edges() order, and counts once toward Exactly or AtLeast,
which assert the size of the whole union whether they are called before or
after Or. An Or with no predicates matches every edge, as Edges() does. The
predicates are copied, so a later change to the caller's slice does not
reach the query. Or returns the receiver for chaining.

<a name="EdgeQuery.SelectEdges"></a>
#### func (\*EdgeQuery) SelectEdges

<pre>func (q *<a href="#EdgeQuery">EdgeQuery</a>) SelectEdges(body *<a href="#Body">Body</a>) ([]*<a href="#Edge">Edge</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

SelectEdges resolves the query against the body's topology: gather
([Body](<#Body>).Edges(), whose order the result keeps), keep each edge that satisfies
every predicate of at least one branch, then enforce the cardinality
assertion on that set (agent-docs/evaluator-design.md §7). A
nil body has no topology to select from and is ErrDegenerate; zero matches
is ErrCardinality when asserted, else ErrNoMatch (core §12 precedence).

<a name="EdgeQuery.String"></a>
#### func (\*EdgeQuery) String

<pre>func (q *<a href="#EdgeQuery">EdgeQuery</a>) String() <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a></pre>

String renders the query canonically:
edges(\<pred\>, \<pred\>, …).or(\<pred\>, …)…\<cardinality\>, one .or(…) per Or
call in call order and the cardinality last. The rendering is a deterministic function of the recorded content — equal
recorded queries render identically, and a query and its decoded round-trip
render identically — built from the codec's own tagged vocabulary. It is an
identity for diagnostics and equality, not a parseable format.

<a name="EdgeSelector"></a>
### type EdgeSelector

<pre>type EdgeSelector interface {

    // SelectEdges resolves the query against a live body&#39;s topology.
    SelectEdges(*<a href="#Body">Body</a>) ([]*<a href="#Edge">Edge</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)
    // contains filtered or unexported methods
}</pre>

EdgeSelector is what an edge-consuming feature (fillet, chamfer) accepts:
an unresolved edge query.

<a name="EdgeWedge"></a>
### type EdgeWedge

<pre>type EdgeWedge <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a></pre>

EdgeWedge is the material wedge across an edge, which [Edge](<#Edge>).Wedge reads.

<a name="WedgeUndecided"></a><a name="WedgeSalient"></a><a name="WedgeReflex"></a>

<pre>const (
    // WedgeUndecided is an edge whose wedge this evaluator does not read, or
    // whose reading its proven normal bounds do not decide.
    WedgeUndecided <a href="#EdgeWedge">EdgeWedge</a> = iota
    // WedgeSalient is an edge whose material angle is under a half turn: a
    // box&#39;s outer edge, a boss&#39;s top rim, a hole&#39;s rim.
    WedgeSalient
    // WedgeReflex is an edge whose material angle is over a half turn: a boss
    // root, an inside corner.
    WedgeReflex
)</pre>

<a name="EdgeWedge.String"></a>
#### func (EdgeWedge) String

<pre>func (w <a href="#EdgeWedge">EdgeWedge</a>) String() <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a></pre>

String returns "undecided", "salient" or "reflex".

<a name="Ellipse3"></a>
### type Ellipse3

<pre>type Ellipse3 struct {
    Center, Axis, Major  r3.Vec
    SemiMajor, SemiMinor units.Value
}</pre>

Ellipse3 is an elliptical arc edge. Major is the unit direction of its
semi-major axis in the plane normal to [Axis](<#Axis>). An edge whose start and end
vertex are one vertex is the whole ellipse.

<a name="EmbossMode"></a>
### type EmbossMode

<pre>type EmbossMode <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a></pre>

EmbossMode says whether a relief stands out of a face or is cut into it.

<a name="EmbossRaised"></a><a name="EmbossEngraved"></a>

<pre>const (
    // EmbossRaised adds the relief on the outward side of the face.
    EmbossRaised <a href="#EmbossMode">EmbossMode</a> = iota
    // EmbossEngraved cuts the relief into the body from the face.
    EmbossEngraved
)</pre>

<a name="EmbossMode.String"></a>
#### func (EmbossMode) String

<pre>func (m <a href="#EmbossMode">EmbossMode</a>) String() <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a></pre>

String names the mode.

<a name="EmbossOption"></a>
### type EmbossOption

<pre>type EmbossOption interface {
    option.Interface
    // contains filtered or unexported methods
}</pre>

EmbossOption configures [Emboss](<#Emboss>).

<a name="WithEmbossDraft"></a>
#### func WithEmbossDraft

<pre>func WithEmbossDraft(angle units.Value) <a href="#EmbossOption">EmbossOption</a></pre>

WithEmbossDraft leans the relief's walls by a draft angle
(agent-docs/emboss-design.md §6). A positive angle makes a raised relief
narrower toward its top and an engraving narrower toward its floor, the way a
moulded or cast part leaves its mould. A negative angle widens them. The angle
is [WithTaper](<#WithTaper>)'s: a draft at or past a right angle is ErrDegenerate, and the
zero value is a straight wall.

<a name="WithEmbossRimFillet"></a>
#### func WithEmbossRimFillet

<pre>func WithEmbossRimFillet(radius units.Value) <a href="#EmbossOption">EmbossOption</a></pre>

WithEmbossRimFillet rounds the relief's rim with a fillet of the given radius
(agent-docs/emboss-design.md §7). The rim of a raised relief is the edges of
its top face, and the rim of an engraving is the edges where its wall meets the
face it is cut into. The radius is a positive length. The relief is built and
filleted on a copy of b first, so a fillet the evaluator refuses leaves b
live and the document unchanged; the copy leaves history entries.

<a name="Exactness"></a>
### type Exactness

<pre>type Exactness = report.<a href="report.md#Exactness">Exactness</a></pre>

Exactness reports whether a measured value is exact or bounded.

<a name="Extent"></a>
### type Extent

<pre>type Extent interface {
    // contains filtered or unexported methods
}</pre>

Extent is what Extrude takes: the sealed linear extent set. No angular
extent satisfies it — "revolve 90mm" is unrepresentable, not a runtime
error.

<a name="ExtrudeOption"></a>
### type ExtrudeOption

<pre>type ExtrudeOption interface {
    option.Interface
    // contains filtered or unexported methods
}</pre>

ExtrudeOption configures Extrude. A chain section accepts none of them: both
WithTaper and WithSurfaceResult return ErrUnsupported on a chain.

<a name="WithTaper"></a>
#### func WithTaper

<pre>func WithTaper(a units.Value) <a href="#ExtrudeOption">ExtrudeOption</a></pre>

WithTaper sets the extrude taper: a SIGNED displacement angle — which way
the wall leans. A positive taper leans every wall into the material as it
leaves the sketch plane, so the body narrows toward the far end; a negative
one widens it (agent-docs/draft-design.md §2). An angle at or past a right angle
is [ErrDegenerate](<#ErrDegenerate>). A nonzero taper builds over [Distance](<#Distance>), [ToFace](<#ToFace>),
[ThroughAll](<#ThroughAll>), [Symmetric](<#Symmetric>) or [TwoSided](<#TwoSided>). WithSurfaceResult is [ErrUnsupported](<#ErrUnsupported>),
returned before commit. A zero taper builds the straight prism. A chain
section returns [ErrUnsupported](<#ErrUnsupported>) for WithTaper at any angle, zero included.

<a name="Face"></a>
### type Face

<pre>type Face struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}</pre>

Face is a topological face: a tagged surface bounded by loops.

<a name="Face.Area"></a>
#### func (\*Face) Area

<pre>func (f *<a href="#Face">Face</a>) Area() (<a href="#Measurement">Measurement</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

Area returns the face's area: Exact only when the result is proved exactly
representable. Analytic float evaluation and boolean-built [Faceted](<#Faceted>) faces
return Approximate with their proven bounds.

<a name="Face.Centroid"></a>
#### func (\*Face) Centroid

<pre>func (f *<a href="#Face">Face</a>) Centroid() (<a href="#VecMeasurement">VecMeasurement</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

Centroid returns the area centroid of a face with a proved certificate.
Point-loft far caps, their planar Split caps and the planar faces of a
SolidFromMesh body provide one; other faces currently return ErrUnsupported.

<a name="Face.ClosestPoint"></a>
#### func (\*Face) ClosestPoint

<pre>func (f *<a href="#Face">Face</a>) ClosestPoint(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, p r3.Vec, tol units.Value) (<a href="#ClosestPoint">ClosestPoint</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

[ClosestPoint](<#ClosestPoint>) finds the point of this face's trimmed patch nearest p. It
reads the triangles a verified mesh attributes to the face, as
[Face](<#Face>).DistanceToPoint does, so Point lies within OffSurface of the patch.
The face may belong to a solid or sheet, including a retired body. tol is
the positive tessellation chord tolerance.

<a name="Face.DistanceToPoint"></a>
#### func (\*Face) DistanceToPoint

<pre>func (f *<a href="#Face">Face</a>) DistanceToPoint(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, p r3.Vec, tol units.Value) (<a href="#Measurement">Measurement</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

DistanceToPoint measures the minimum distance in millimetres from p to this
face's trimmed patch. The face may belong to a solid or sheet, including a
retired body. tol is the positive tessellation chord tolerance. A verified
two-sided face displacement bounds the returned measurement.

<a name="Face.Edges"></a>
#### func (\*Face) Edges

<pre>func (f *<a href="#Face">Face</a>) Edges() []*<a href="#Edge">Edge</a></pre>

Edges returns the face's edges across all loops.

<a name="Face.Loops"></a>
#### func (\*Face) Loops

<pre>func (f *<a href="#Face">Face</a>) Loops() []*<a href="#Loop">Loop</a></pre>

Loops returns the face's boundary loops, the outer loop first.

<a name="Face.NormalAt"></a>
#### func (\*Face) NormalAt

<pre>func (f *<a href="#Face">Face</a>) NormalAt(p r3.Vec) (<a href="#VecMeasurement">VecMeasurement</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

NormalAt returns the face's outward normal at p. Its bound combines the
arithmetic proof for the normal of the face's tagged surface
(normal\_bound.go) and any proven departure of the surface actually carried
from that tag (normalBound). A revolve wall's or cap's bound is instead
proven against the surface its record denotes (topo.Face.Denoted), which covers
its tag's departure and the arm's arithmetic at once. It is Exact only when the
whole bound is zero. A point that gives the surface no direction is
ErrDegenerate. A reading whose own enclosure cannot separate the direction
from zero is ErrUnsupported.

The five analytic variants — [Plane](<#Plane>), [Cylinder](<#Cylinder>), [Cone](<#Cone>), [Sphere](<#Sphere>) and [Torus](<#Torus>) — are
the whole set this answers for. Any other tagged surface is ErrUnsupported:
a [NURBSSurface](<#NURBSSurface>) for the reason agent-docs/spline-design.md §7 owns, and a [Faceted](<#Faceted>)
face — the tag every boolean-produced face carries — because its answer
waits on the faceted certificate stage
(agent-docs/payload-verification-design.md §5.4, §13).

<a name="Face.Origins"></a>
#### func (\*Face) Origins

<pre>func (f *<a href="#Face">Face</a>) Origins() []<a href="#FeatureRef">FeatureRef</a></pre>

Origins returns every feature role that created this face —
canonicalization may merge coplanar faces, and a merged face carries ALL
contributing roles (core §6.1). A face of an analytic Boolean result also
carries the roles of the one operand face it provably lies inside
(agent-docs/prism-boolean-design.md §11).

<a name="Face.Surface"></a>
#### func (\*Face) Surface

<pre>func (f *<a href="#Face">Face</a>) Surface() <a href="#Surface">Surface</a></pre>

[Surface](<#Surface>) returns the face's tagged geometry.

<a name="FaceHistory"></a>
### type FaceHistory

<pre>type FaceHistory struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}</pre>

FaceHistory contains the known output faces derived from one input face.

<a name="FaceHistory.Coverage"></a>
#### func (FaceHistory) Coverage

<pre>func (h <a href="#FaceHistory">FaceHistory</a>) Coverage() <a href="#HistoryCoverage">HistoryCoverage</a></pre>

[Coverage](<#Coverage>) reports whether Faces lists every successor for this input face.

<a name="FaceHistory.Faces"></a>
#### func (FaceHistory) Faces

<pre>func (h <a href="#FaceHistory">FaceHistory</a>) Faces() []*<a href="#Face">Face</a></pre>

Faces returns a copy of the known successor faces.

<a name="FacePredicate"></a>
### type FacePredicate

<pre>type FacePredicate struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}</pre>

FacePredicate is one clause of a [FaceQuery](<#FaceQuery>). Predicates come
only from the package constructors — Planar, Cylindrical, NormalTo,
Facing, FaceCreatedBy — and compose by conjunction within a branch
([FaceQuery](<#FaceQuery>).Or adds a branch); the zero value names no predicate and is
rejected at resolve.

<a name="Cylindrical"></a>
#### func Cylindrical

<pre>func Cylindrical() <a href="#FacePredicate">FacePredicate</a></pre>

Cylindrical matches faces whose surface is a cylinder. On a [Faceted](<#Faceted>) body
the analytic identity is gone, so it matches nothing there — matching is
decided on what the face IS (agent-docs/evaluator-design.md §7).

<a name="FaceCreatedBy"></a>
#### func FaceCreatedBy

<pre>func FaceCreatedBy(f <a href="#FeatureRef">FeatureRef</a>) <a href="#FacePredicate">FacePredicate</a></pre>

FaceCreatedBy matches faces by provenance — the face analog of CreatedBy.
A canonicalization merge unions the merged faces' roles and this matches
on any of them, so provenance survives the merge
(agent-docs/evaluator-design.md §3). A negative producer identity or empty role is rejected at
resolve as ErrDegenerate.

<a name="Facing"></a>
#### func Facing

<pre>func Facing(v r3.Vec) <a href="#FacePredicate">FacePredicate</a></pre>

Facing matches the planar face whose OUTWARD (material-leaving) normal points
ALONG v — parallel to v AND the same sense, a positive projection. NormalTo
matches on either sense, so a slab's two parallel caps both match NormalTo(z);
Facing(z) picks only the top one. The vector is recorded exactly as given — a
dimensionless direction (core §5.2); a degenerate (zero or non-finite)
direction is rejected at resolve, not here.

<a name="NormalTo"></a>
#### func NormalTo

<pre>func NormalTo(v r3.Vec) <a href="#FacePredicate">FacePredicate</a></pre>

NormalTo matches planar faces whose normal is parallel to v. The vector is
recorded exactly as given — a dimensionless direction (core §5.2); a
degenerate (zero or non-finite) direction is rejected at resolve, not here.

<a name="Planar"></a>
#### func Planar

<pre>func Planar() <a href="#FacePredicate">FacePredicate</a></pre>

Planar matches faces whose surface is a plane.

<a name="Walls"></a>
#### func Walls

<pre>func Walls(b *<a href="#Body">Body</a>) <a href="#FacePredicate">FacePredicate</a></pre>

Walls matches every face a sweep made: the faces carrying a side(i, j) role
of b's own producing feature. It is the sibling of CapStart and CapEnd, and
it is what Draft takes as the complete wall set of an extrude
(agent-docs/draft-design.md §10). On a body whose producer mints no side roles it
matches nothing, an ordinary ErrNoMatch at resolve. b must not be nil.

<a name="FaceQuery"></a>
### type FaceQuery

<pre>type FaceQuery struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}</pre>

FaceQuery is the concrete face selector: a union of branches, each a
conjunction of face predicates, plus an optional cardinality assertion over
the union. Build one with Faces and add branches with Or.

<a name="Faces"></a>
#### func Faces

<pre>func Faces(preds ...<a href="#FacePredicate">FacePredicate</a>) *<a href="#FaceQuery">FaceQuery</a></pre>

Faces returns a query matching every face that satisfies all of preds; no
predicates matches every face. A query that matches nothing at resolve is
an error, loudly — ErrNoMatch, or ErrCardinality when asserted (core §9).

<a name="FaceQuery.AtLeast"></a>
#### func (\*FaceQuery) AtLeast

<pre>func (q *<a href="#FaceQuery">FaceQuery</a>) AtLeast(n <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a>) *<a href="#FaceQuery">FaceQuery</a></pre>

AtLeast asserts the query resolves to at least n matches; fewer is
ErrCardinality at resolve. It replaces any earlier cardinality assertion
and returns the receiver for chaining.

<a name="FaceQuery.Exactly"></a>
#### func (\*FaceQuery) Exactly

<pre>func (q *<a href="#FaceQuery">FaceQuery</a>) Exactly(n <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a>) *<a href="#FaceQuery">FaceQuery</a></pre>

Exactly asserts the query resolves to exactly n matches; anything else —
zero included — is ErrCardinality at resolve. It replaces any earlier
cardinality assertion and returns the receiver for chaining.

<a name="FaceQuery.Or"></a>
#### func (\*FaceQuery) Or

<pre>func (q *<a href="#FaceQuery">FaceQuery</a>) Or(preds ...<a href="#FacePredicate">FacePredicate</a>) *<a href="#FaceQuery">FaceQuery</a></pre>

Or adds a union branch: the query then also matches every face that
satisfies all of preds. A face that several branches match is selected
once, in [Body](<#Body>).Faces() order, and counts once toward Exactly or AtLeast,
which assert the size of the whole union whether they are called before or
after Or. An Or with no predicates matches every face, as Faces() does. The
predicates are copied, so a later change to the caller's slice does not
reach the query. Or returns the receiver for chaining.

Faces(FaceCreatedBy(CapStart(b))).Or(FaceCreatedBy(CapEnd(b))).Exactly(2)
names both angular caps of a partial-turn revolve b, which no single
conjunction of geometric predicates names when the caps are not coplanar.

<pre>func (q *<a href="#FaceQuery">FaceQuery</a>) SelectFaces(body *<a href="#Body">Body</a>) ([]*<a href="#Face">Face</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

SelectFaces resolves the query against the body's topology: gather
([Body](<#Body>).Faces(), whose order the result keeps), keep each face that satisfies
every predicate of at least one branch, then enforce the cardinality
assertion on that set (agent-docs/evaluator-design.md §7). A
nil body has no topology to select from and is ErrDegenerate; zero matches
is ErrCardinality when asserted, else ErrNoMatch (core §12 precedence).

<a name="FaceQuery.String"></a>
#### func (\*FaceQuery) String

<pre>func (q *<a href="#FaceQuery">FaceQuery</a>) String() <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a></pre>

String renders the query canonically:
faces(\<pred\>, \<pred\>, …).or(\<pred\>, …)…\<cardinality\>, the face analog of
[EdgeQuery](<#EdgeQuery>).String.

<a name="FaceSelector"></a>
### type FaceSelector

<pre>type FaceSelector interface {

    // SelectFaces resolves the query against a live body&#39;s topology.
    SelectFaces(*<a href="#Body">Body</a>) ([]*<a href="#Face">Face</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)
    // contains filtered or unexported methods
}</pre>

FaceSelector is what a face-consuming feature (shell) accepts: an
unresolved face query. It embeds the sealed selector root, so every
selector a feature accepts is recordable (core §9/§6.2).

<a name="FaceShell"></a>
### type FaceShell

<pre>type FaceShell struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}</pre>

FaceShell is a connected set of faces.

<a name="FaceShell.Faces"></a>
#### func (\*FaceShell) Faces

<pre>func (s *<a href="#FaceShell">FaceShell</a>) Faces() []*<a href="#Face">Face</a></pre>

Faces returns the shell's faces.

<a name="FaceShell.IsOpen"></a>
#### func (\*FaceShell) IsOpen

<pre>func (s *<a href="#FaceShell">FaceShell</a>) IsOpen() <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#bool">bool</a></pre>

IsOpen reports whether the shell has at least one free edge
(agent-docs/surface-design.md §2.2). IsOpen and IsVoid are independent questions
and neither implies the other. A solid's shell is never open; a
surface-result feature's sheet shell reports true wherever its build
omitted a closing face and left a rim with no second face to pair it with
(extrude.go, internal/revolveplan/build.go), and false for a closed sheet that mints no
such rim — a full revolution (agent-docs/surface-design.md Table W).

<a name="FaceShell.IsVoid"></a>
#### func (\*FaceShell) IsVoid

<pre>func (s *<a href="#FaceShell">FaceShell</a>) IsVoid() <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#bool">bool</a></pre>

IsVoid reports whether the shell bounds an internal cavity. IsVoid and
IsOpen are independent questions and neither implies the other
(agent-docs/surface-design.md §2.2): a void solid shell and an open sheet shell
are both ordinary states, and nothing rules out either combination.

Faceted marks a polygonal face. Bound encloses the displacement from its

<a name="Faceted.Kind"></a>
#### func (Faceted) Kind

<pre>func (<a href="#Faceted">Faceted</a>) Kind() <a href="#SurfaceKind">SurfaceKind</a></pre>

Kind reports KindFaceted.

### type FacetedCurve

<pre>type FacetedCurve struct{ Bound units.Value }</pre>

FacetedCurve is a polygonal edge. Bound encloses the displacement from its
