<a name="FeatureRef"></a>
### type FeatureRef

<pre>type FeatureRef struct {

    // Role names the entity within the producing feature: &#34;side(i,j)&#34; (loop i, segment
    // j), &#34;capStart&#34;, &#34;capEnd&#34;, &#34;body&#34;.
    Role <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a>
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}</pre>

FeatureRef identifies the stable role that created a body, face, or edge.
The producing operation is tracked privately so callers cannot forge or
depend on document-local operation identities.

<a name="CapEnd"></a>
#### func CapEnd

<pre>func CapEnd(b *<a href="#Body">Body</a>) <a href="#FeatureRef">FeatureRef</a></pre>

CapEnd names the end-cap role of b's own producing feature — the sibling of
CapStart. A body whose feature mints no end cap (a cup, a full revolution) still
gets a well-formed ref that matches nothing.

<a name="CapStart"></a>
#### func CapStart

<pre>func CapStart(b *<a href="#Body">Body</a>) <a href="#FeatureRef">FeatureRef</a></pre>

CapStart names the start-cap role of b's own producing feature, so
FaceCreatedBy(CapStart(b)) selects that cap without a "capStart" string
literal a typo could break. It reads b.Origin().producer (§6) and pairs it with
the fixed role. The role exists only where the feature mints it — an extrude, a
partial revolve, a shell that built a tube, an authenticated axial
Loft/cylinder join or its centered bore Cut, or a Transform/Copy
of one; on any other body the ref is still well-formed and simply matches
nothing (an ordinary ErrNoMatch at resolve). An ordinary mesh boolean
preserves only its operands' cap origins, so name those with
FaceCreatedBy(CapStart(originalBody)).

<a name="FilletChamferOption"></a>
### type FilletChamferOption

<pre>type FilletChamferOption interface {
    <a href="#FilletOption">FilletOption</a>
    <a href="#ChamferOption">ChamferOption</a>
}</pre>

FilletChamferOption is accepted by both Fillet and Chamfer.

<a name="WithTangentChain"></a>
#### func WithTangentChain

<pre>func WithTangentChain() <a href="#FilletChamferOption">FilletChamferOption</a></pre>

WithTangentChain expands each selected seed edge across the edges that
continue it with proven G1 continuity (agent-docs/modify-reach-design.md §5): an
edge leaving the seed's endpoint along the exactly opposite tangent ray,
whose two adjacent faces have the same outward normals there as the
seed's. The expansion repeats from every edge it adds. The seed query's
cardinality assertion applies to the seeds, before expansion. A
continuation with more than one candidate, or one this evaluator cannot
decide, is ErrUnsupported; the call never picks a branch or stops early.
Repeating the option is the same as passing it once.

<a name="HoleShape"></a>
### type HoleShape

<pre>type HoleShape interface {
    // contains filtered or unexported methods
}</pre>

HoleShape is the cross-section of a hole that is not round. Its variants are
[RectangularHole](<#RectangularHole>), [SlotHole](<#SlotHole>), [PolygonHole](<#PolygonHole>) and [OutlineHole](<#OutlineHole>).

<a name="HoleSpec"></a>
### type HoleSpec

<pre>type HoleSpec struct {
    Face     <a href="#FaceSelector">FaceSelector</a>
    At       r3.Vec
    Diameter units.Value
    Depth    <a href="#HoleDepth">HoleDepth</a>
    Head     <a href="#HoleHead">HoleHead</a>
    Shape    <a href="#HoleShape">HoleShape</a>
    Thread   *<a href="#HoleThread">HoleThread</a>
    Draft    units.Value
}</pre>

HoleSpec describes one hole.

[Face](<#Face>) selects the face the hole starts in and must resolve to exactly one
face, an analytic plane or cylinder. At is a world point in millimetres that
lies on that face's plane, or on the cylinder; the hole axis runs through it,
into the body, square to the plane or along the cylinder's radius. Diameter is a length. Depth is
required. Head is optional, and nil makes a plain hole; on a cylindrical face it cuts
from the plane tangent there (agent-docs/hole-design.md §11).

Shape is optional. A nil Shape makes a round hole of Diameter. A non-nil
Shape replaces the round bore: Diameter MUST then be the zero units.Value and
Head MUST be nil, each otherwise ErrDegenerate.

Thread is optional. A non-nil Thread taps the round bore in the same commit
(agent-docs/hole-design.md §8). It needs a nil Shape, ErrDegenerate otherwise.
On a cylindrical face the thread starts at the tangent plane at At, and the
cut is the evaluator's own ErrUnsupported where it cannot hold the pair
(agent-docs/hole-design.md §12).

Draft is optional and leans the round bore's wall (agent-docs/hole-design.md
§9): a positive angle makes the bore narrower toward its bottom, a negative one
wider, and the zero Value is a straight bore. Diameter is the bore's diameter
at the face either way. It needs a nil Shape and a nil Thread, each otherwise
ErrDegenerate, and a planar face, ErrUnsupported on a cylinder. An angle whose
magnitude is at or past a right angle is ErrDegenerate, and one that closes the
bore before its bottom is the drafted extrusion's own refusal.

<a name="HoleThread"></a>
### type HoleThread

<pre>type HoleThread struct {
    Pitch    units.Value
    LeftHand <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#bool">bool</a>
    Length   units.Value
}</pre>

HoleThread is a thread tapped into a round hole. The hole's Diameter is then
the thread's minor (tap drill) diameter. Pitch is the axial advance per turn,
a positive length. The thread is right-handed unless LeftHand is set. Length
is the length to thread, measured from where the bore proper starts (the face
of a plain hole, the floor of a counterbore or the bottom of a countersink): the
zero Value threads the bore's whole length, running out of a through hole's far
end, and a positive length no longer than the bore stops the thread there with
the coil's flat end (agent-docs/hole-design.md §8).

<a name="WithCellBudget"></a>
#### func WithCellBudget

<pre>func WithCellBudget(cells <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a>) <a href="#JointBoxOption">JointBoxOption</a></pre>

WithCellBudget caps the number of cell centres VerifyJointBox evaluates
(agent-docs/linkage-check-design.md §14.4); the default is 16384. Every split
evaluates two centres, so once fewer than two evaluations remain no cell is
split and the report raises DiagJointBoxBudgetExhausted. A budget of 1
evaluates the whole box's centre alone; cells \< 1 is decaderr.ErrDegenerate. It is a
[JointBoxOption](<#JointBoxOption>) only, so VerifyMotion and VerifyLinkage do not accept it.

<a name="LatticeSpec"></a>
### type LatticeSpec

<pre>type LatticeSpec struct {
    // Min and Max are the box&#39;s corners in millimetres; Min is below Max on every
    // axis.
    Min, Max r3.Vec
    // Cell is the length after which the lattice repeats along each axis, a
    // positive length.
    Cell units.Value
    // Level is a dimensionless wall thickness: the solid is where the lattice&#39;s
    // field g lies within Level of zero, |g| ≤ Level. The gyroid&#39;s g runs from
    // −3/2 to 3/2, so a level of 0.3 gives a thin wall, 1 a heavy one and values
    // near 3/2 a nearly full box; the Schwarz-P field runs from −3 to 3 and the
    // diamond&#39;s from −√2 to √2, the Neovius field from −13 to 13, the IWP field
    // from −5 to 3, the Fischer-Koch S field from −√2 to √2 and the Lidinoid from −1.35 to 1.15 and the Split P from −1.8 to about 1.81. Level lies strictly between 0 and the field&#39;s largest absolute
    // value (agent-docs/lattice-design.md §4).
    Level units.Value
    // Resolution is the number of samples to a cell along each axis, from 4 up.
    // The zero value takes 16. A finer grid follows the surface more closely and
    // makes more triangles.
    Resolution <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a>
}</pre>

LatticeSpec describes a lattice for [GyroidLattice](<#GyroidLattice>), [SchwarzPLattice](<#SchwarzPLattice>),
[DiamondLattice](<#DiamondLattice>), [NeoviusLattice](<#NeoviusLattice>), [IWPLattice](<#IWPLattice>), [FischerKochSLattice](<#FischerKochSLattice>), [LidinoidLattice](<#LidinoidLattice>) and [SplitPLattice](<#SplitPLattice>).

<a name="LoftFacesOption"></a>
### type LoftFacesOption

<pre>type LoftFacesOption interface {
    option.Interface
    // contains filtered or unexported methods
}</pre>

LoftFacesOption configures LoftFaces. An option from another package cannot
implement this sealed tier.

<a name="WithConeTangentEnd"></a>
#### func WithConeTangentEnd

<pre>func WithConeTangentEnd(cone *<a href="#Body">Body</a>, radial r3.Vec) <a href="#LoftFacesOption">LoftFacesOption</a></pre>

WithConeTangentEnd ends the loft with a last, constructed section tangent
to cone along one ruling (agent-docs/loft-face-sections-design.md,
"[Cone](<#Cone>)-tangent end section").

The cone is a live, unplaced, full straight-meridian Revolve cone about
world X. radial is the direction of the touching ruling's radius: its X
must be 0 and its (Y, Z) finite and nonzero. The last section is built from
the cone, not selected. Its plane is exactly tangent to the cone's exact
apex and slope, with the source origin at the cone apex, so it fits a
point-loft source whose plane is that tangent plane. Any other source still
goes through the ordinary embedding gates, which refuse an inconsistent end.
The end face carries the cap-end role of the new loft and a rounded [Plane](<#Plane>)
tag. Cut and Intersect continue from the result as they do without the
option.

The option is accepted at most once. With it, LoftFaces takes 1 to 31 cap
faces. The cone must be live in the document of the first section's body.

<a name="LoftOption"></a>
### type LoftOption

<pre>type LoftOption interface {
    option.Interface
    // contains filtered or unexported methods
}</pre>

LoftOption configures Loft.

<a name="WithLoftAlignment"></a>
#### func WithLoftAlignment

<pre>func WithLoftAlignment(offsets ...<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a>) <a href="#LoftOption">LoftOption</a></pre>

WithLoftAlignment records, per loop, which recorded segment index of the
SECOND profile pairs with segment index 0 of the FIRST profile's
corresponding loop. offsets\[0\] is the outer loop; offsets\[1+h\] is
p1.Holes\[h\]. Omitting the option means every offset is 0 — the natural
case where both profiles were authored with matching segment order
(agent-docs/loft-design.md §2/§3 Table P row P4).

The option is accepted at most once: two payloads are two different
correspondences, so a repeat is [ErrDegenerate](<#ErrDegenerate>) rather than last-wins
(Table S row S4).

<a name="WithLoftSplits"></a>
#### func WithLoftSplits

<pre>func WithLoftSplits(first, second []<a href="#LoftSplit">LoftSplit</a>) <a href="#LoftOption">LoftOption</a></pre>

WithLoftSplits cuts recorded segments of the first and of the second section
before the loft pairs them, so two sections whose loops hold different numbers
of segments can be paired one to one. Each piece is the same recorded curve over
a sub-range of the segment's own parameter range, the way a trimmed fragment is
recorded, so a split changes no curve. A fraction f resolves to the parameter
TStart + f·(TEnd − TStart) of the segment, which is proportional to length on a
line and a parameter of the curve on any other kind. The pieces follow each
other in the loop's walk order. WithLoftAlignment then applies to the split
loops, and a wall's source role names the split segment index.

The option is accepted at most once, like WithLoftAlignment: two payloads are
two different correspondences, so a repeat is [ErrDegenerate](<#ErrDegenerate>). A split index
outside its loop, a fraction outside (0, 1) or not increasing, a segment split
twice, and a fraction that rounds onto its neighbour are [ErrDegenerate](<#ErrDegenerate>) too.
Loops still holding different segment counts, or a pair still of different
kinds, after the splits are [ErrUnsupported](<#ErrUnsupported>) as without the option, and a
correspondence that twists is refused by the crossing audit.

<a name="MeasuredProfile.SecondMoments"></a>
#### func (MeasuredProfile) SecondMoments

<pre>func (p <a href="#MeasuredProfile">MeasuredProfile</a>) SecondMoments() (<a href="#SecondMoments">SecondMoments</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

[SecondMoments](<#SecondMoments>) measures area moments about the sketch plane's origin.

<a name="Measurement"></a>
### type Measurement

<pre>type Measurement = report.<a href="report.md#Measurement">Measurement</a></pre>

Measurement is a scalar value with its exactness and absolute error bound.

<a name="Mesh"></a>
### type Mesh

<pre>type Mesh struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}</pre>

Mesh is a triangle mesh: an OUTPUT of [Body.Tessellate](<#Body.Tessellate>), never the body
representation (core §3 invariant #1 — the public vocabulary stays
[Body](<#Body>) → [Face](<#Face>) → [Edge](<#Edge>) → [Vertex](<#Vertex>)). Vertices lie on the evaluator's held boundary;
curve chording and inherited payload displacement are bounded by Bound. A Mesh
is immutable: the accessors return copies of its slices.

<a name="Mesh.Bound"></a>
#### func (\*Mesh) Bound

<pre>func (m *<a href="#Mesh">Mesh</a>) Bound() units.Value</pre>

Bound returns the proven deviation bound: no point of the body's boundary
lies farther than this from the mesh, and vice versa. It is the largest
complete displacement the tessellation used, including curve chording and
inherited payload coordinate bounds. Its chording component is at most the
requested tolerance — it is a PROVEN upper bound on the chord-to-arc
deviation rather than that deviation itself, so it can read above the
deviation a chord actually takes by the factor [Body.Tessellate](<#Body.Tessellate>) states;
inherited payload displacement is added on top, so
Bound can exceed that tolerance. It is zero only when every held boundary
coordinate is exact. A scalar quantity is a units.Value (core §5.1): Kind
Length, millimetres.

<a name="Mesh.BoundaryVerified"></a>
#### func (\*Mesh) BoundaryVerified

<pre>func (m *<a href="#Mesh">Mesh</a>) BoundaryVerified() <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#bool">bool</a></pre>

BoundaryVerified reports whether every boundary audit this body's payload
supports ran and passed — including, on a payload that carries one, the
facet-contact audit that proves the facet set embedded and free of
non-adjacent contact (agent-docs/tessellation-design.md §1's Embedding row).

It is false exactly when [VerifyNone](<#VerifyNone>) was asked of a payload whose boundary
proof includes that audit. Every other boundary audit — directed-edge
closure or the manifold-with-boundary audit, vertex links, per-facet
positive area, signed-volume orientation — runs at every level, so no other
payload's reading moves with the level.

<a name="Mesh.SourceFaces"></a>
#### func (\*Mesh) SourceFaces

<pre>func (m *<a href="#Mesh">Mesh</a>) SourceFaces() []*<a href="#Face">Face</a></pre>

SourceFaces returns, parallel to Triangles, the analytic face each facet
approximates — the provenance the mesh boolean groups its output by
(agent-docs/evaluator-design.md §9). The elements are the body's live faces.

<a name="Mesh.Triangles"></a>
#### func (\*Mesh) Triangles

<pre>func (m *<a href="#Mesh">Mesh</a>) Triangles() [][3]<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a></pre>

Triangles returns the facets as index triples into Vertices, wound
counter-clockwise seen from outside the body. On a [BodySheet](<#BodySheet>) there is no
"outside": the winding is counter-clockwise seen from the shell's own
positive side (agent-docs/surface-design.md §2.3) — the same side [Face.NormalAt](<#Face.NormalAt>)
answers on for a wall the solid the sheet came from would have carried. The
indices describe the mesh's own connectivity; they are not selectors
(core §3 invariant #3).

"Outside the body" presupposes an EMBEDDED surface, which is what the
facet-contact audit proves, so the word holds as a geometric statement only
when [Mesh.BoundaryVerified](<#Mesh.BoundaryVerified>) is true. On a mesh built below [VerifyBoundary](<#VerifyBoundary>)
the winding is still consistent across every shared edge and still outward
under the construction's own convention — the signed-volume orientation
audit runs at every level — but a self-intersecting closed mesh can carry a
positive signed volume while having points where "outside" names nothing.
For a renderer culling back faces or lighting them the two readings agree;
for a caller who needs the guarantee, ask for it.

<a name="Mesh.Vertices"></a>
#### func (\*Mesh) Vertices

<pre>func (m *<a href="#Mesh">Mesh</a>) Vertices() []r3.Vec</pre>

Vertices returns the mesh vertex positions in millimetres (core §5.2).
Every vertex lies on the held boundary. Its deviation from the denoted body,
including inherited payload displacement, is covered by Bound.

<a name="Mesh.VolumeVerified"></a>
#### func (\*Mesh) VolumeVerified

<pre>func (m *<a href="#Mesh">Mesh</a>) VolumeVerified() <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#bool">bool</a></pre>

VolumeVerified reports whether this mesh carries the proof of the volume it
and the body it stands for differ by (agent-docs/tessellation-design.md §2's
volSymDiff). It is what admits the mesh to [Union](<#Union>), [Cut](<#Cut>) and [Intersect](<#Intersect>).

It is false below [VerifyAll](<#VerifyAll>), where that proof never ran, and false at
[VerifyAll](<#VerifyAll>) too for a body whose payload class publishes no occupied-volume
proof at all — a cap-loop chamfer whose band has a mitered circular wall or
a reflex corner, a sheet, or a stitched body whose vertices are not proven
exact. A false reading is the proof's ABSENCE, never
a bound of zero: a zero would be the claim that the mesh occupies exactly
the denoted volume.

<a name="MeshBody"></a>
### type MeshBody

<pre>type MeshBody struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}</pre>

MeshBody is an imported triangle mesh (agent-docs/mesh-import-design.md). It
NEVER claims to be a solid B-rep: its triangles are the whole of what it
knows, it has no faces, edges or analytic surfaces, and no feature or Boolean
takes it. It reads out what the triangles say: bounds, area, and the volume of
a closed, consistently wound mesh, each as an exact or bounded measurement of
the mesh itself. It is immutable.

<a name="DiamondLattice"></a>
#### func DiamondLattice

<pre>func DiamondLattice(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, spec <a href="#LatticeSpec">LatticeSpec</a>) (*<a href="#MeshBody">MeshBody</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

DiamondLattice builds a Schwarz diamond lattice, the field
sin kx·sin ky·sin kz + sin kx·cos ky·cos kz + cos kx·sin ky·cos kz +
cos kx·cos ky·sin kz, whose solid is where \|g\| ≤ Level, as a closed
[MeshBody](<#MeshBody>) filling the box of spec (agent-docs/lattice-design.md §4).
Everything GyroidLattice says holds, except that the field runs from −√2 to √2
and Level lies strictly between 0 and √2.

<a name="FischerKochSLattice"></a>
#### func FischerKochSLattice

<pre>func FischerKochSLattice(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, spec <a href="#LatticeSpec">LatticeSpec</a>) (*<a href="#MeshBody">MeshBody</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

FischerKochSLattice builds a Fischer-Koch S lattice, the field
cos 2kx·sin ky·cos kz + cos kx·cos 2ky·sin kz + sin kx·cos ky·cos 2kz, whose solid is where
\|g\| ≤ Level, as a closed [MeshBody](<#MeshBody>) filling the box of spec (agent-docs/lattice-design.md §4). Everything
GyroidLattice says holds, except that the field runs from −√2 to √2 and Level lies strictly between 0 and √2.

<a name="GyroidLattice"></a>
#### func GyroidLattice

<pre>func GyroidLattice(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, spec <a href="#LatticeSpec">LatticeSpec</a>) (*<a href="#MeshBody">MeshBody</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

GyroidLattice builds a gyroid lattice, the triply periodic wall used for
lightweight print infill, as a closed [MeshBody](<#MeshBody>) filling the box of spec
(agent-docs/lattice-design.md). The box's faces cap the lattice, so the mesh
is closed and wound outward, and its [MeshBody.Volume](<#MeshBody.Volume>) reads.

The surface is the zero set of the field sampled on a grid and cut by
marching tetrahedra, so it is as exact as the grid is fine: the mesh is not a
B-rep, and its volume converges on the lattice's as Resolution grows. The
lattice fills a box, not a body: nothing here takes a mesh body into a Boolean.

ctx MUST NOT be nil. A nil context, a box with no volume, a cell that is not
positive, a level not between 0 and 3/2 (the gyroid field's largest value), a Resolution below 4, and a lattice
that needs more than 8 million samples or 2 million triangles are
ErrDegenerate. A cell of the wrong unit kind is ErrUnitKind and a negative one
ErrNegativeMagnitude. A level that is not dimensionless is ErrUnitKind.
Non-finite corners are ErrNotFinite. A canceled context returns its error.

<a name="IWPLattice"></a>
#### func IWPLattice

<pre>func IWPLattice(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, spec <a href="#LatticeSpec">LatticeSpec</a>) (*<a href="#MeshBody">MeshBody</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

IWPLattice builds an I-graph and wrapped package (IWP) lattice, the field
2(cos kx·cos ky + cos ky·cos kz + cos kz·cos kx) − (cos 2kx + cos 2ky + cos 2kz),
whose solid is where \|g\| ≤ Level, as a closed [MeshBody](<#MeshBody>) filling the box of
spec (agent-docs/lattice-design.md §4). Everything GyroidLattice says holds,
except that the field runs from −5 to 3, so Level lies strictly between 0 and
5, the largest \|g\|.

<a name="LidinoidLattice"></a>
#### func LidinoidLattice

<pre>func LidinoidLattice(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, spec <a href="#LatticeSpec">LatticeSpec</a>) (*<a href="#MeshBody">MeshBody</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

LidinoidLattice builds a Lidinoid lattice, the field
½(sin 2kx·cos ky·sin kz + sin 2ky·cos kz·sin kx + sin 2kz·cos kx·sin ky) −
½(cos 2kx·cos 2ky + cos 2ky·cos 2kz + cos 2kz·cos 2kx) + 0.15, whose solid is where \|g\| ≤ Level, as a closed
[MeshBody](<#MeshBody>) filling the box of spec (agent-docs/lattice-design.md §4). Everything GyroidLattice says holds, except
that the field runs from −1.35 to 1.15, so Level lies strictly between 0 and 1.35, the largest \|g\|.

<a name="NeoviusLattice"></a>
#### func NeoviusLattice

<pre>func NeoviusLattice(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, spec <a href="#LatticeSpec">LatticeSpec</a>) (*<a href="#MeshBody">MeshBody</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

NeoviusLattice builds a Neovius lattice, the field
3(cos kx + cos ky + cos kz) + 4 cos kx·cos ky·cos kz, whose solid is where
\|g\| ≤ Level, as a closed [MeshBody](<#MeshBody>) filling the box of spec
(agent-docs/lattice-design.md §4). Everything GyroidLattice says holds, except
that the field runs from −13 to 13 and Level lies strictly between 0 and 13.

<a name="NewMeshBody"></a>
#### func NewMeshBody

<pre>func NewMeshBody(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, vertices []r3.Vec, triangles [][3]<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a>) (*<a href="#MeshBody">MeshBody</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

NewMeshBody builds a mesh body from vertices in millimetres and triangles as
index triples into them. The triangles wind counter-clockwise seen from
outside the body they enclose. vertices and triangles are copied.

A nil context is ErrDegenerate. A mesh with no triangle is ErrDegenerate. A
vertex that is not finite, or a triangle index outside vertices, is
ErrUnsupported. NewMeshBody welds and repairs nothing: whatever the
triangles say is what [MeshBody.Report](<#MeshBody.Report>) reports. A canceled context returns
its error.

<a name="ReadIGES"></a>
#### func ReadIGES

<pre>func ReadIGES(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, r io.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/io#Reader">Reader</a>, opts ...<a href="#MeshImportOption">MeshImportOption</a>) (*<a href="#MeshBody">MeshBody</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

ReadIGES reads the planar-faced solids of an IGES file into a [MeshBody](<#MeshBody>)
(agent-docs/format-io-design.md). It reads every manifold solid B-rep entity (186) with the shells (514),
faces (510), loops (508), edge lists (504) and vertex lists (502) below it: each face on a plane
(108, 190) is cut into triangles, a face with holes included, the vertices are welded by coordinate and
each solid is wound outward, a void's shell into its cavity. Lengths are converted from the file's unit to
millimetres.

Only planes with straight line edges (110) are read. A face on any other surface, a curved edge, a vertex
entry in a loop, an entity placed by a transformation matrix, a scaled model space, and a file that holds
only surfaces and curves with no B-rep, are [ErrUnsupported](<#ErrUnsupported>). A file that is not well-formed IGES, or whose
entities do not make the B-rep they name (a loop that does not close, a shell whose faces are not
two-sided), is \[ErrMalformed\], and input past a limit is [ErrMeshTooLarge](<#ErrMeshTooLarge>). The mesh is only the file's
own faces: nothing is repaired, so [SolidFromMesh](<#SolidFromMesh>) decides whether it is a solid.

ctx and r MUST NOT be nil, each otherwise ErrDegenerate. A canceled context returns its error.

<a name="ReadOBJ"></a>
#### func ReadOBJ

<pre>func ReadOBJ(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, r io.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/io#Reader">Reader</a>, opts ...<a href="#MeshImportOption">MeshImportOption</a>) (*<a href="#MeshBody">MeshBody</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

ReadOBJ reads a Wavefront OBJ file into a [MeshBody](<#MeshBody>)
(agent-docs/mesh-import-design.md). Only the "v" vertex and "f" face lines
count. A face index is positive (from 1) or negative (back from the latest
vertex), and any "/" part after the vertex is ignored. A face of more than
three vertices is cut into a fan from its first vertex, which is right for a
convex face and wrong for any other. Coordinates are millimetres. Vertices
with identical coordinates are welded and nothing else is repaired.

ctx and r MUST NOT be nil, each otherwise ErrDegenerate. Malformed input is
[ErrMalformedMesh](<#ErrMalformedMesh>) and input past a limit is [ErrMeshTooLarge](<#ErrMeshTooLarge>). A canceled
context returns its error.

<a name="ReadSTEP"></a>
#### func ReadSTEP

<pre>func ReadSTEP(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, r io.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/io#Reader">Reader</a>, opts ...<a href="#MeshImportOption">MeshImportOption</a>) (*<a href="#MeshBody">MeshBody</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

ReadSTEP reads the planar-, cylinder- and cone-faced solids of a STEP file into a [MeshBody](<#MeshBody>)
(agent-docs/format-io-design.md). It reads every MANIFOLD\_SOLID\_BREP and
BREP\_WITH\_VOIDS: each face on a plane is cut into triangles, a face with holes
included, each wall on a cylinder or a cone is cut into a ladder of triangles, arcs are
cut into chords within 0.01 mm of their circle, and the vertices are welded
by coordinate. A cavity's shell winds
into the cavity, so the volume of a solid with one reads as the material
alone. Lengths are converted from the file's unit to millimetres.

Only planes, cylinders, cones and sphere caps, with straight and circular edges, are read. A
face on a torus or free-form surface, a sphere face other than a cap with one circular bound, a cone at its apex, a wall with
holes or an oblique boundary, or an edge that is an ellipse or a curve, is
[ErrUnsupported](<#ErrUnsupported>). A file that is
not well-formed STEP, or whose entities do not make the B-rep they name, is
[ErrMalformedMesh](<#ErrMalformedMesh>), and input past a limit is [ErrMeshTooLarge](<#ErrMeshTooLarge>).

ctx and r MUST NOT be nil, each otherwise ErrDegenerate. A canceled context
returns its error.

<a name="ReadSTL"></a>
#### func ReadSTL

<pre>func ReadSTL(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, r io.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/io#Reader">Reader</a>, opts ...<a href="#MeshImportOption">MeshImportOption</a>) (*<a href="#MeshBody">MeshBody</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

ReadSTL reads a binary or ASCII STL file into a [MeshBody](<#MeshBody>)
(agent-docs/mesh-import-design.md). A file is binary when its length is
exactly 84 bytes plus 50 for each triangle its count names, and ASCII when it
starts with "solid". Facet normals and attributes are ignored: a triangle's
side comes from its vertex order. Coordinates are millimetres. Vertices with
identical coordinates are welded and nothing else is repaired.

ctx and r MUST NOT be nil, each otherwise ErrDegenerate. Malformed input is
[ErrMalformedMesh](<#ErrMalformedMesh>) and input past a limit is [ErrMeshTooLarge](<#ErrMeshTooLarge>). A canceled
context returns its error.

<a name="ReadThreeMF"></a>
#### func ReadThreeMF

<pre>func ReadThreeMF(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, r io.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/io#Reader">Reader</a>, opts ...<a href="#MeshImportOption">MeshImportOption</a>) (*<a href="#MeshBody">MeshBody</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

ReadThreeMF reads a 3MF package into a [MeshBody](<#MeshBody>)
(agent-docs/mesh-import-design.md §8). Every build item that is not a support
is read: its mesh, or the meshes of its components, moved by the transforms on
the item and its components and scaled from the model's unit to millimetres.
Vertices with identical coordinates are welded and nothing else is repaired.
Materials, colours, textures and other extensions are ignored.

A transform must be rigid: a rotation, a translation or a reflection. A
transform that scales or shears is [ErrUnsupported](<#ErrUnsupported>).

ctx and r MUST NOT be nil, each otherwise ErrDegenerate. A package that is
not a well-formed 3MF model is [ErrMalformedMesh](<#ErrMalformedMesh>) and input past a limit,
including a part that expands past the byte limit, is [ErrMeshTooLarge](<#ErrMeshTooLarge>). A
canceled context returns its error.

<a name="RefineMesh"></a>
#### func RefineMesh

<pre>func RefineMesh(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, m *<a href="#MeshBody">MeshBody</a>, maxEdge units.Value) (*<a href="#MeshBody">MeshBody</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

RefineMesh splits the long edges of m and returns the result as a new
[MeshBody](<#MeshBody>) (agent-docs/mesh-import-design.md §11). m is not changed.

Every edge longer than maxEdge is cut at its midpoint, and each triangle is
cut along its split edges, again and again until no edge is longer. Both
triangles on a shared edge take the same new vertex, so a closed mesh stays
closed, its winding is kept and its orientation readings stand. No vertex of m
moves, so the mesh covers the same surface: its area and volume are those of m,
to the exactness of the arithmetic, and the refinement adds triangles and no
shape. Use it before a step that needs short edges, such as a finer
tessellation to scale or reduce. A mesh with no long edge comes back as a copy.

ctx and m MUST NOT be nil, each otherwise ErrDegenerate. maxEdge is a positive
length: zero is ErrDegenerate, a negative value ErrNegativeMagnitude and a
wrong unit kind ErrUnitKind. A refinement that needs over five million
triangles, or whose edges are still long after 40 rounds, is ErrUnsupported. A
canceled context returns its error.

<a name="RemeshMesh"></a>
#### func RemeshMesh

<pre>func RemeshMesh(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, m *<a href="#MeshBody">MeshBody</a>, edge units.Value) (*<a href="#MeshBody">MeshBody</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

RemeshMesh rebuilds the closed mesh m from near-equilateral triangles with edges near edge, and returns the result
as a new [MeshBody](<#MeshBody>) (agent-docs/mesh-import-design.md §14). m is not changed.

It makes eight passes of incremental isotropic remeshing: split the edges longer than 4/3 of edge, merge the edges
shorter than 4/5 of it, flip edges toward six neighbours to a vertex, and slide each vertex toward its neighbours'
centroid along the surface. Every step keeps the surface closed, manifold and wound as m is, and refuses a move
that would turn a triangle by about 78 degrees or more. The vertices are not projected back onto m, so a convex
surface shrinks a little in each pass and the result stands within a few per cent of m's volume, with no proven
distance; a thin feature narrower than edge can pinch or pass through itself.

ctx and m MUST NOT be nil, each otherwise ErrDegenerate. edge is a positive length: zero is ErrDegenerate, a
negative value ErrNegativeMagnitude and a wrong unit kind ErrUnitKind. A mesh that is not closed, consistently
wound and manifold is ErrUnsupported, and so is an edge so short that the result would pass a million triangles.
A canceled context returns its error.

<a name="ScaleBodyMesh"></a>
#### func ScaleBodyMesh

<pre>func ScaleBodyMesh(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, b *<a href="#Body">Body</a>, anchor r3.Vec, x, y, z, tol units.Value, opts ...<a href="#TessellateOption">TessellateOption</a>) (*<a href="#MeshBody">MeshBody</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

ScaleBodyMesh stretches a solid body by a separate factor along each world
axis about anchor and returns the result as a [MeshBody](<#MeshBody>)
(agent-docs/mesh-import-design.md §10). The solid kernel has no per-axis
scale: [ScaledAt](<#ScaledAt>) is uniform and [Transform](<#Transform>) is rigid, and a stretched sphere
is no sphere. So b is tessellated at chord tolerance tol, and the mesh is
stretched as [ScaleMesh](<#ScaleMesh>) stretches one. b is not changed.

The result is a mesh of the stretched solid, not a [Body](<#Body>): no feature takes it,
but it reads, queries and exports as a mesh does. Its volume is that of the
tessellation times \|x·y·z\|, so it holds the volume of b to the tessellation's
own error, which tol bounds for a curved body and which is nil for a body of
flat faces. opts are [Body.Tessellate](<#Body.Tessellate>)'s. ctx and b MUST NOT be nil; the other
gates, with those of tol, are ScaleMesh's and Tessellate's, and a sheet or a
body that will not tessellate is Tessellate's refusal.

<a name="ScaleMesh"></a>
#### func ScaleMesh

<pre>func ScaleMesh(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, m *<a href="#MeshBody">MeshBody</a>, anchor r3.Vec, x, y, z units.Value) (*<a href="#MeshBody">MeshBody</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

ScaleMesh stretches m by a separate factor along each world axis about anchor
and returns the result as a new [MeshBody](<#MeshBody>) (agent-docs/mesh-import-design.md
§10). m is not changed.

Every vertex p moves to anchor + (p − anchor) scaled by x, y and z along the
axes. A uniform stretch is a similarity, and any other is not: it turns a
sphere into an ellipsoid and tilts every face that is not square to an axis.
The volume of a closed mesh is multiplied by \|x·y·z\|, and an area by no one
factor.

A negative factor mirrors the mesh across the plane through anchor square to
that axis. An odd number of negative factors would turn the triangles inside
out, so their corners are reordered to keep a closed mesh wound outward and
its [MeshBody.Volume](<#MeshBody.Volume>) positive.

ctx and m MUST NOT be nil, each otherwise ErrDegenerate. Each factor is
dimensionless, finite and not zero: a wrong unit kind is ErrUnitKind, a
non-finite factor or anchor ErrNotFinite and a zero factor ErrDegenerate. A
result whose vertices overflow is ErrNotFinite, and a triangle too large to
bound its area ErrUnsupported. A canceled context returns its
error.

<a name="SchwarzPLattice"></a>
#### func SchwarzPLattice

<pre>func SchwarzPLattice(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, spec <a href="#LatticeSpec">LatticeSpec</a>) (*<a href="#MeshBody">MeshBody</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

SchwarzPLattice builds a Schwarz primitive (P) lattice, cos kx + cos ky + cos kz,
a triply periodic wall of cubic symmetry whose solid is where \|g\| ≤ Level, as a
closed [MeshBody](<#MeshBody>) filling the box of spec (agent-docs/lattice-design.md §4).
Everything GyroidLattice says holds, except that the field runs from −3 to 3 and
Level lies strictly between 0 and 3.

<a name="SplitPLattice"></a>
#### func SplitPLattice

<pre>func SplitPLattice(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, spec <a href="#LatticeSpec">LatticeSpec</a>) (*<a href="#MeshBody">MeshBody</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

SplitPLattice builds a Split P lattice, the field
1\.1(sin 2kx·sin kz·cos ky + sin 2ky·sin kx·cos kz + sin 2kz·sin ky·cos kx) −
0\.2(cos 2kx·cos 2ky + cos 2ky·cos 2kz + cos 2kz·cos 2kx) − 0.4(cos 2kx + cos 2ky + cos 2kz), whose solid is where
\|g\| ≤ Level, as a closed [MeshBody](<#MeshBody>) filling the box of spec (agent-docs/lattice-design.md §4). Everything
GyroidLattice says holds, except that the field runs from −1.8 to about 1.81 and Level lies strictly between 0 and
1\.8.

<a name="SubDMesh"></a>
#### func SubDMesh

<pre>func SubDMesh(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, cage <a href="#SubDCage">SubDCage</a>, levels <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a>) (*<a href="#MeshBody">MeshBody</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

SubDMesh refines a polygon cage into its Catmull-Clark subdivision surface, a
smooth shape drawn by moving the cage's vertices, as the Form workspace of a
CAD system sculpts one, and returns it as a [MeshBody](<#MeshBody>) (agent-docs/subd-design.md).
Each of levels rounds replaces every n-gon by n quads and moves the vertices
by the Catmull-Clark rules, so the mesh converges on the limit surface, which
lies inside a convex cage. A closed cage gives a
closed mesh whose [MeshBody.Volume](<#MeshBody.Volume>) reads, and an open cage gives an open mesh
whose boundary keeps to the limit of the cage's boundary curve.

levels is from 1 to 8, and no round may make more than 1,000,000 quads,
otherwise ErrDegenerate. The cage must be a manifold of polygons: an edge used by more than
two faces, two faces that walk an edge the same way, a face of fewer than three
distinct vertices or naming a vertex that is not there, an interior vertex in fewer
than three faces, and a boundary vertex that does not touch exactly two boundary
edges are ErrDegenerate. A vertex that is not finite is ErrNotFinite, and a nil
context is ErrDegenerate.

<a name="MeshBody.Area"></a>
#### func (\*MeshBody) Area

<pre>func (m *<a href="#MeshBody">MeshBody</a>) Area() (<a href="#Measurement">Measurement</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

Area returns the total area of the triangles. Each triangle's area is a
square root, so the reading is Approximate with a proven bound, except where
every root is exact.

<a name="MeshBody.Bounds"></a>
#### func (\*MeshBody) Bounds

<pre>func (m *<a href="#MeshBody">MeshBody</a>) Bounds() <a href="#Box">Box</a></pre>

Bounds returns the axis-aligned box of the vertices. It is Exact: the
vertices are the mesh. A vertex that no triangle uses still counts.

<a name="MeshBody.ClosestPoint"></a>
#### func (\*MeshBody) ClosestPoint

<pre>func (m *<a href="#MeshBody">MeshBody</a>) ClosestPoint(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, p r3.Vec) (<a href="#ClosestPoint">ClosestPoint</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

[ClosestPoint](<#ClosestPoint>) finds the point of the closed mesh's region nearest p: p itself
when it lies inside or on the mesh, and otherwise the nearest point of the
nearest triangle, rounded to floats. Its OffSurface is that rounding alone.
Errors are LocatePoint's.

<a name="MeshBody.DistanceToPoint"></a>
#### func (\*MeshBody) DistanceToPoint

<pre>func (m *<a href="#MeshBody">MeshBody</a>) DistanceToPoint(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, p r3.Vec) (<a href="#Measurement">Measurement</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

DistanceToPoint measures the minimum distance in millimetres from p to the
region the closed mesh encloses: zero for a point inside or on it, and
otherwise the distance to the nearest triangle. The reading is computed in
exact arithmetic from the mesh itself, so it carries only the rounding of
the float it is published as. Errors are LocatePoint's.

<a name="MeshBody.LocatePoint"></a>
#### func (\*MeshBody) LocatePoint

<pre>func (m *<a href="#MeshBody">MeshBody</a>) LocatePoint(ctx context.<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/context#Context">Context</a>, p r3.Vec) (<a href="#PointLocation">PointLocation</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

LocatePoint classifies p against the region the closed mesh encloses
(agent-docs/mesh-import-design.md §5). The answer is exact, with no
tolerance: a ray crossing count over the triangles decides inside from
outside, and a point on a triangle is PointOnBoundary. Where the mesh crosses
itself the count decides, so a region covered twice reads as outside. The
mesh need not wind counter-clockwise seen from outside: an inverted mesh
encloses the same region. A mesh that is not closed is ErrNotSolid. A nil
context or mesh is ErrDegenerate, and a point that is not finite is
ErrNotFinite.

<a name="MeshBody.Report"></a>
#### func (\*MeshBody) Report

<pre>func (m *<a href="#MeshBody">MeshBody</a>) Report() <a href="#MeshReport">MeshReport</a></pre>

[Report](<#Report>) returns what the triangles say about the mesh.

<a name="MeshBody.Triangles"></a>
#### func (\*MeshBody) Triangles

<pre>func (m *<a href="#MeshBody">MeshBody</a>) Triangles() [][3]<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a></pre>

Triangles returns the triangles as index triples into Vertices. The slice is
a copy.

<a name="MeshBody.Vertices"></a>
#### func (\*MeshBody) Vertices

<pre>func (m *<a href="#MeshBody">MeshBody</a>) Vertices() []r3.Vec</pre>

Vertices returns the vertex positions in millimetres. The slice is a copy.

<a name="MeshBody.Volume"></a>
#### func (\*MeshBody) Volume

<pre>func (m *<a href="#MeshBody">MeshBody</a>) Volume() (<a href="#Measurement">Measurement</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

Volume returns the volume the mesh encloses. It is ErrNotSolid unless the
mesh is closed and wound counter-clockwise seen from outside: a mesh with a
boundary edge, a non-manifold or misoriented edge, or a negative signed
volume encloses no volume the triangles can state. The reading is the exact
sum of signed tetrahedra, so it is Exact when that sum is representable and
otherwise carries only the rounding of its float value.

<a name="MeshBoundError"></a>
### type MeshBoundError

<pre>type MeshBoundError = decaderr.MeshBoundError</pre>

MeshBoundError is Tessellate's refusal of a chord tolerance finer than the
minimum mesh bound a faceted body holds. Every tolerance at or above Floor
restates the same held facets, so a caller may retry at exactly Floor.
errors.As(err, \&target) with target a \*MeshBoundError reads it, and
errors.Is(err, [ErrUnsupported](<#ErrUnsupported>)) keeps holding.

<a name="MeshReduceReport"></a>
### type MeshReduceReport

<pre>type MeshReduceReport struct {
    // MergedVertices counts the vertices that shared a cell with an earlier one,
    // and DroppedTriangles the triangles that collapsed to fewer than three
    // cells or repeated another triangle.
    MergedVertices, DroppedTriangles <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a>
    // MaxVertexMove is the greatest distance from an original vertex to the
    // vertex that replaced it. It bounds how far the vertices moved, and is not a
    // bound on how far the surface moved: a triangle can fold or pass through
    // others as its corners move.
    MaxVertexMove units.Value
    // SurfaceBound is set by [ReduceMeshWithin] and is the zero Value after [ReduceMesh]. It is a
    // proven bound on the distance between the input surface and the result, in both directions.
    SurfaceBound units.Value
}</pre>

MeshReduceReport states what [ReduceMesh](<#ReduceMesh>) changed.

<a name="MeshRepairOption"></a>
### type MeshRepairOption

<pre>type MeshRepairOption interface {
    option.Interface
    // contains filtered or unexported methods
}</pre>

MeshRepairOption configures [RepairMesh](<#RepairMesh>).

<a name="WithMeshFillHoles"></a>
#### func WithMeshFillHoles

<pre>func WithMeshFillHoles() <a href="#MeshRepairOption">MeshRepairOption</a></pre>

WithMeshFillHoles closes each simple boundary loop, one whose every vertex
has one way onward along the boundary. A loop of three is closed with one
triangle and a longer one with a fan from a new vertex at the loop's centroid.
The caps are flat only when the loop is, so a bent loop closes to a surface
that need not match the part it came from. A boundary that branches is left
open and counted in [MeshRepairReport](<#MeshRepairReport>).SkippedLoops.

<a name="WithMeshOrient"></a>
#### func WithMeshOrient

<pre>func WithMeshOrient() <a href="#MeshRepairOption">MeshRepairOption</a></pre>

WithMeshOrient winds every shell consistently and turns a closed shell that
is inside out right way out. Shells are the groups of triangles that meet
along edges which exactly two triangles use; an edge that three or more
triangles use joins nothing.

<a name="WithMeshWeld"></a>
#### func WithMeshWeld

<pre>func WithMeshWeld(distance units.Value) <a href="#MeshRepairOption">MeshRepairOption</a></pre>

WithMeshWeld merges vertices that lie within distance of one another into the
earliest of them. distance is a non-negative length; zero merges only vertices
at identical coordinates. A near-equal pair that straddles a seam is joined,
so the seam closes, and a pair of distinct features closer than distance is
joined too: pick a distance well below the mesh's finest detail.

<a name="MeshRepairReport"></a>
### type MeshRepairReport

<pre>type MeshRepairReport struct {
    // WeldedVertices counts the vertices merged into an earlier one.
    WeldedVertices <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a>
    // DroppedTriangles counts the triangles removed: those that name a vertex
    // twice, have zero area, or repeat an earlier triangle&#39;s vertices.
    DroppedTriangles <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a>
    // FlippedTriangles counts the triangles whose winding was reversed.
    FlippedTriangles <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a>
    // FilledLoops counts the boundary loops closed, and SkippedLoops the
    // connected runs of boundary left open because they branch.
    FilledLoops, SkippedLoops <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a>
    // AddedTriangles counts the triangles the fills added.
    AddedTriangles <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a>
}</pre>

MeshRepairReport counts what [RepairMesh](<#RepairMesh>) changed.

<a name="MeshReport"></a>
### type MeshReport

<pre>type MeshReport struct {
    // Vertices and Triangles count the input.
    Vertices, Triangles <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a>
    // DegenerateTriangles counts triangles of zero area, including those that
    // name a vertex twice. They add no area or volume and join no shell.
    DegenerateTriangles <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a>
    // BoundaryEdges counts edges that exactly one triangle uses.
    BoundaryEdges <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a>
    // NonManifoldEdges counts edges that three or more triangles use.
    NonManifoldEdges <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a>
    // MisorientedEdges counts edges that exactly two triangles use in the same
    // direction.
    MisorientedEdges <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a>
    // Shells counts connected groups of triangles joined across shared edges.
    Shells <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a>
    // Closed reports a mesh whose every edge is used by exactly two triangles
    // in opposite directions.
    Closed <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#bool">bool</a>
    // Inverted reports a closed mesh whose signed volume is negative, that is
    // one wound clockwise seen from outside.
    Inverted <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#bool">bool</a>
}</pre>

MeshReport states what a [MeshBody](<#MeshBody>)'s triangles say about it. The counts are
read from the triangles alone; none of them depends on a tolerance.

<a name="MirrorFace"></a>
### type MirrorFace

<pre>type MirrorFace struct {
    Body *<a href="#Body">Body</a>
    Face <a href="#FaceSelector">FaceSelector</a>
}</pre>

MirrorFace mirrors across a planar face of [Body](<#Body>), selected and never pointed
at (core §9). [Body](<#Body>) is what [Face](<#Face>) resolves against: it MUST be a live body of
the same document as the receiver (ErrForeignBody, ErrRetiredBody), and the
receiver itself is the ordinary choice. Resolving the plane does not consume
[Body](<#Body>).

[Face](<#Face>) resolves through SelectFaces([Body](<#Body>)) under the implicit exactly-one rule:
zero or several faces is ErrCardinality with Expected "exactly 1", and a
failed assertion of the selector's own is returned unchanged. A curved face
is ErrDegenerate. A flat face with no analytic [Plane](<#Plane>) surface, such as a
mesh-boolean [Faceted](<#Faceted>) face, states no exact plane and is ErrUnsupported.
The mirror plane is the face's own [Plane](<#Plane>).Frame. Under [WithJoin](<#WithJoin>), [Body](<#Body>) must
be the receiver and [Face](<#Face>) may name several walls on one line: zero faces is
ErrCardinality with Expected "at least 1".

<a name="MirrorFrame"></a>
### type MirrorFrame

<pre>type MirrorFrame struct {
    Frame r3.Frame
}</pre>

MirrorFrame mirrors across the plane through Frame's origin spanned by its
U and V axes, the plane r3.Reflection takes. The zero Frame names no plane
and is ErrDegenerate at the call.

<a name="MirrorOption"></a>
### type MirrorOption

<pre>type MirrorOption interface {
    // contains filtered or unexported methods
}</pre>

MirrorOption configures [Mirrored](<#Mirrored>). [WithJoin](<#WithJoin>) is the one option.

<a name="WithJoin"></a>
#### func WithJoin

<pre>func WithJoin() <a href="#MirrorOption">MirrorOption</a></pre>

WithJoin makes [Mirrored](<#Mirrored>) return the union of the receiver and its
mirror image as one body: the symmetric-part operation
(agent-docs/mirror-pattern-design.md §5). The plane must be a [MirrorFace](<#MirrorFace>) of the
receiver itself naming one or more planar walls on one line of its section;
the selector then asserts at least one face rather than exactly one.

The join rewrites the receiver's own recorded section and never runs a
boolean. It admits a straight prism or a stacked prism (a blind-cut plate)
whose every other boundary segment is a whole line, a whole arc or a whole
circle lying on the receiver's side of the mirror line, and whose recorded
section carries no displacement. Every other receiver is refused with the
sentinel §5.1 states — ErrUnsupported for a shape the join does not build,
ErrDegenerate for a selection that names no single mirror line — and is
never handed to Union instead. A repeated WithJoin() is idempotent.

MirrorPlane is what a body may be mirrored across: a [MirrorFrame](<#MirrorFrame>) the
caller builds, or a [MirrorFace](<#MirrorFace>) naming a planar face of a body. The set is
sealed (agent-docs/mirror-pattern-design.md §4.1).

}</pre>

NeutralFace names a planar face of [Body](<#Body>), selected and never pointed at
(core §9), under [MirrorFace](<#MirrorFace>)'s rules: [Face](<#Face>) resolves through
SelectFaces([Body](<#Body>)) under the implicit exactly-one rule, so zero or several
faces is [ErrCardinality](<#ErrCardinality>) with Expected "exactly 1"; a curved face is
[ErrDegenerate](<#ErrDegenerate>); a flat face with no analytic [Plane](<#Plane>) surface, such as a
mesh-boolean [Faceted](<#Faceted>) face, is [ErrUnsupported](<#ErrUnsupported>). [Body](<#Body>) MUST be a live body
of b's document ([ErrForeignBody](<#ErrForeignBody>), [ErrRetiredBody](<#ErrRetiredBody>)). This
evaluator drafts about a cap of b only, so [Body](<#Body>) must be

<a name="PathPatternOption"></a>
### type PathPatternOption

<pre>type PathPatternOption interface {
    option.Interface
    // contains filtered or unexported methods
}</pre>

PathPatternOption configures [PathPattern](<#PathPattern>).

<a name="WithPathCount"></a>
#### func WithPathCount

<pre>func WithPathCount(n <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a>) <a href="#PathPatternOption">PathPatternOption</a></pre>

WithPathCount makes [PathPattern](<#PathPattern>) place n instances, b and n-1 copies, at
equal arc length along the path. The first is at the path's start and the
last at its end (agent-docs/path-pattern-design.md §1). n is at least 2, and
a smaller n is ErrDegenerate. A call takes exactly one of WithPathCount and
[WithPathSpacing](<#WithPathSpacing>).

<a name="WithPathFollow"></a>
#### func WithPathFollow

<pre>func WithPathFollow() <a href="#PathPatternOption">PathPatternOption</a></pre>

WithPathFollow turns each copy of [PathPattern](<#PathPattern>) to follow the path.
Copy i is rotated about the path's start by the shortest turn that takes the
path's direction of travel there onto its direction at that copy's point,
then moved to the point. The body is taken to sit at the path's start with
its own forward along the path. A path that comes back on itself, so that
the direction at a point is exactly opposite the start's, is ErrDegenerate:
that turn has no shortest axis.

<a name="WithPathPivot"></a>
#### func WithPathPivot

<pre>func WithPathPivot(pivot r3.Vec) <a href="#PathPatternOption">PathPatternOption</a></pre>

WithPathPivot turns each copy about pivot, a point in millimetres, instead of
about the path's start. It sets the point that [WithPathFollow](<#WithPathFollow>)'s turn
leaves in place before the copy is moved to its station, so a body that sits
away from the path's start, or a pivot at the body's own centre, swings
about that point. The last of several pivots wins. A pivot with no
[WithPathFollow](<#WithPathFollow>) has no turn to centre and is ErrDegenerate, and a non-finite
pivot is ErrNotFinite.

<a name="WithPathSpacing"></a>
#### func WithPathSpacing

<pre>func WithPathSpacing(spacing units.Value) <a href="#PathPatternOption">PathPatternOption</a></pre>

WithPathSpacing makes [PathPattern](<#PathPattern>) place instances spacing apart by arc
length. Instance i sits i·spacing along the path, for every i within its
length, and a spacing that divides the length puts the last instance at the
path's end (agent-docs/path-pattern-design.md §6). spacing is a positive
length no longer than the path. A wrong unit kind is ErrUnitKind and a
negative spacing is ErrNegativeMagnitude. A zero spacing, one that leaves no
copy, and one that would place over 100000 copies are ErrDegenerate. A call
takes exactly one of WithPathSpacing and [WithPathCount](<#WithPathCount>).

<a name="RevolveOption"></a>
### type RevolveOption

<pre>type RevolveOption interface {
    option.Interface
    // contains filtered or unexported methods
}</pre>

RevolveOption configures Revolve. WithSurfaceResult (agent-docs/surface-design.md
§4) is the one option today: it omits the two caps a partial sweep would
otherwise close with and publishes a sheet instead of a solid. A full
revolution mints no closing face to omit, so there the option changes no
face and returns a CLOSED sheet with no free edge — §2.1's closed-sheet
rule, not a refusal (Table W). A repeated WithSurfaceResult() is
idempotent, never an error. A chain section always revolves to a sheet, so
Revolve returns ErrUnsupported for WithSurfaceResult() on a chain.

<a name="RibOption"></a>
### type RibOption

<pre>type RibOption interface {
    // contains filtered or unexported methods
}</pre>

RibOption configures WebPath. WithRibOverrun and WithRibDraft make one.

<a name="WithRibDraft"></a>
#### func WithRibDraft

<pre>func WithRibDraft(angle units.Value) <a href="#RibOption">RibOption</a></pre>

WithRibDraft leans the rib's walls by a draft angle
(agent-docs/rib-design.md §7). A positive angle makes the rib thinner as it
rises from the plane of the sketch, the way a moulded or cast rib releases
from its tool, and a negative one thicker. The angle is [WithTaper](<#WithTaper>)'s, so the
lean is measured from the sketch plane, the ends lean too, and a draft at or
past a right angle is ErrDegenerate. The last occurrence wins and the default
is a straight wall. A rib whose outline has a corner that an arc meets, such
as an arc rib of [WebPath](<#WebPath>), takes the refusals of the drafted [Extrude](<#Extrude>) it builds.

<a name="WithRibOverrun"></a>
#### func WithRibOverrun

<pre>func WithRibOverrun(overrun units.Value) <a href="#RibOption">RibOption</a></pre>

WithRibOverrun lengthens every rib by overrun beyond both ends of its line or
arc, measured along the arc for an arc rib. A rib whose ends only touch a wall of the body is a coplanar contact that
the union refuses, so a rib that spans a cavity draws its line wall to wall
and adds an overrun to bury both ends in the walls. overrun is a
non-negative length, and the last occurrence wins. The default is zero.

<a name="SecondMoments"></a>
### type SecondMoments

<pre>type SecondMoments struct {
    // UU is ∫u² dA, VV is ∫v² dA, and UV is ∫uv dA.
    UU  <a href="#Measurement">Measurement</a>
    UV  <a href="#Measurement">Measurement</a>
    VV  <a href="#Measurement">Measurement</a>
}</pre>

SecondMoments is a region's bounded second moments of area about the plane
origin. Each reading has Kind SecondMomentOfArea (mm⁴). Re-reference them to
another axis with the region's Area and Centroid.

The readings come from the mass-property engine of agent-docs/evaluator-design.md
§4. sketch decides topology and admissibility; internal/momentregion
integrates admitted records by closed-form boundary integrals (Green's
theorem). Line and Tier A free-form walks (agent-docs/spline-design.md Table F)
integrate to exact rationals, so a region built only from them is published
as its own rational rounded ONCE and retains a zero bound wherever that
rational is representable; circular evaluations have no exact rational and
carry outward bounds instead. Every other free-form kind is unsupported.
The engine composes internal/proofbound/bounded.go (the bounded-scalar
arithmetic every published reading is composed in),
internal/proofbound/rat\_interval.go (the exact rational interval arithmetic
the certified terms are proven in) and internal/circularbounds/moments.go
(the circular segment's own enclosures).

<a name="Section"></a>
### type Section

<pre>type Section interface {
    *sketch.Profile | *sketch.Chain
}</pre>

Section is the sketch geometry a section-fed operation consumes: a closed
[\*sketch.Profile](<https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/lestrrat-3d/sketch#Profile>) or an open [\*sketch.Chain](<https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/lestrrat-3d/sketch#Chain>). An operation declared as
func Op\[S Section\](..., sec S, ...) infers S from the argument, so callers
pass either kind without naming the type argument. The operation decides
what each kind builds and which options it accepts; a kind or option the
operation cannot honour returns ErrUnsupported, and a nil section returns
ErrDegenerate.

<a name="SectionClearance"></a>
### type SectionClearance

<pre>type SectionClearance struct {
    // Distance is the polyline clearance in millimetres, zero when Overlaps is
    // true or the outlines touch. Its Bound is the sum of both outlines&#39;
    // OffSurface, the rounding of the arithmetic and the plane tolerance, so
    // the true clearance of the sections lies within Value +/- Bound only to
    // the extent OffSurface does (see Lower).
    Distance <a href="#Measurement">Measurement</a>
    // A is the point of the first outline&#39;s loops, and B the point of the
    // second&#39;s, that attain Distance. Both are in world millimetres. Where
    // the outlines cross or one lies inside the other they are one point.
    A, B r3.Vec
    // Overlaps is true when a loop of one outline properly crosses a loop of
    // the other, or a loop of one lies strictly inside the other&#39;s material.
    // Outlines that merely touch or coincide read Distance zero with Overlaps
    // false.
    Overlaps <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#bool">bool</a>
}</pre>

SectionClearance is the least distance between the material two
[SectionOutline](<#SectionOutline>) values enclose in their shared plane, read from their
polylines (agent-docs/section-outline-design.md §5).

<a name="SectionClearance.Lower"></a>
#### func (SectionClearance) Lower

<pre>func (c <a href="#SectionClearance">SectionClearance</a>) Lower() units.Value</pre>

Lower returns the smallest clearance the reading allows: [Distance](<#Distance>) less its
Bound, and not below zero. A caller may read a certified gap from the
outlines only when Lower is positive. Lower is zero when Overlaps is true.

<a name="SectionOutline"></a>
### type SectionOutline

<pre>type SectionOutline struct {
    // Plane is the cutting plane. Its normal decides each outline&#39;s direction.
    Plane r3.Frame
    // Loops are the closed polylines, in world coordinates in millimetres, the
    // last point joining the first. An outer loop runs counter-clockwise seen
    // from the tip of the plane&#39;s normal and a hole runs clockwise.
    Loops [][]r3.Vec
    // OffSurface bounds how far every point of every loop lies from the body&#39;s
    // true boundary and from the plane: the mesh&#39;s proven displacement bound
    // plus the rounding of the cut&#39;s own arithmetic.
    OffSurface units.Value
}</pre>

SectionOutline is the closed outlines where a body's tessellation meets a
plane (agent-docs/section-outline-design.md). It is a reading of the mesh,
not of the exact solid, and it is not a sketch: nothing in it can enter a
feature as an exact profile.

<a name="SectionOutline.Clearance"></a>
#### func (SectionOutline) Clearance

<pre>func (s <a href="#SectionOutline">SectionOutline</a>) Clearance(other <a href="#SectionOutline">SectionOutline</a>) (<a href="#SectionClearance">SectionClearance</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

[Clearance](<#Clearance>) returns the least distance between the material region this
outline encloses and the one other encloses, both seen in the one plane
(agent-docs/section-outline-design.md §5). Outer loops enclose material and
holes remove it. When the regions overlap the clearance is zero and
Overlaps is true; otherwise it is the least distance between any two
segments of the two outlines, found with bounding-box trees so that two
outlines of thousands of segments take milliseconds.

The Bound of the reading is the sum of both outlines' OffSurface plus the
rounding of the arithmetic. It bounds how far the loop points lie from the
true surface. It does not bound how far the true sections' outlines lie
from the loops where the plane meets the surface at a shallow angle
(section-outline design §2), and a gap is certified only when Lower is
positive.

The two outlines' planes must be the same frame: origin, U and V agree
within 1e-9 (millimetres in the origin, and in each component of the
unit axes). Otherwise, an outline without a loop, a loop of fewer than three
points or a point that is not finite, the result is ErrDegenerate.

<a name="SectionOutline.PolygonArea"></a>
#### func (SectionOutline) PolygonArea

<pre>func (s <a href="#SectionOutline">SectionOutline</a>) PolygonArea() units.Value</pre>

PolygonArea returns the area the loops enclose, an outer loop counted
positive and a hole negative. It is the area of the polygons, so it differs
from the true section's area by an amount OffSurface does not bound: the true
section can differ in outline by far more than OffSurface where the plane
meets the surface at a shallow angle.

<pre>type SheetMetalReport struct {
    // FlatLength is the length of the blank the strip is cut from: the legs plus each bend&#39;s allowance.
    FlatLength units.Value
    // BendAllowances are the lengths of the neutral axis through each bend, angle times (InnerRadius +
    // KFactor·Thickness), in the order of Bends.
    BendAllowances []units.Value
}</pre>

SheetMetalReport states the flat pattern of a strip [SheetMetal](<#SheetMetal>) built.

<a name="SheetMetalSpec"></a>
### type SheetMetalSpec

<pre>type SheetMetalSpec struct {
    // Thickness of the sheet, a positive length.
    Thickness units.Value
    // InnerRadius is the radius of every bend on its inside face, a positive length.
    InnerRadius units.Value
    // Width of the strip across the bends, the length of every bend line, a positive length.
    Width units.Value
    // KFactor places the neutral axis, as a fraction of the thickness from the inside face, in (0, 1]. The
    // zero Value takes 0.44. It sets the flat pattern&#39;s length and not the part&#39;s shape.
    KFactor units.Value
    // Legs are the lengths of the flat portions, in order, each a positive length measured from one bend&#39;s end
    // to the next bend&#39;s start (the first leg from the strip&#39;s end).
    Legs []units.Value
    // Bends are the angles the strip turns between neighbouring legs, one fewer than Legs: a positive angle
    // turns it counter-clockwise in the strip&#39;s plane and a negative one clockwise, each nonzero and less than
    // a half turn.
    Bends []units.Value
}</pre>

SheetMetalSpec describes a bent strip of sheet metal (agent-docs/sheet-metal-design.md): flat legs joined
by circular bends of one inside radius, all of one thickness, a constant Width across.

<a name="ShellOption"></a>
### type ShellOption

<pre>type ShellOption interface {
    // contains filtered or unexported methods
}</pre>

ShellOption configures Shell, including its wall sense.

<a name="WithNoOpenings"></a>
#### func WithNoOpenings

<pre>func WithNoOpenings() <a href="#ShellOption">ShellOption</a></pre>

WithNoOpenings asks Shell to keep every face and build a closed hollow body
(agent-docs/modify-reach-design.md §9.2). It is the only call form in which Shell
accepts a nil face selector, and a non-nil selector beside it is
ErrDegenerate. No receiver builds a closed shell yet: Shell returns
ErrUnsupported for every receiver it accepts the option on.

<a name="WithShellFaceThickness"></a>
#### func WithShellFaceThickness

<pre>func WithShellFaceThickness(normal r3.Vec, t units.Value) <a href="#ShellOption">ShellOption</a></pre>

WithShellFaceThickness gives the walls whose outward normal is the world axis direction normal (+X, +Y, +Z or a
negative one) the thickness t in place of Shell's own, so a part can have a heavy floor and thin sides
(agent-docs/orthogonal-design.md). It applies to an Inward shell of a faceted solid whose faces all square to a
world axis; any other body, a sense other than Inward, a normal that is not exactly a world axis direction
(ErrDegenerate) and a direction named twice (ErrDegenerate) are refused. t is a positive length. Directions the
option does not name take Shell's thickness, and the walls of two directions meet in a mitred corner.

<a name="WithShellSense"></a>
#### func WithShellSense

<pre>func WithShellSense(s <a href="#ShellSense">ShellSense</a>) <a href="#ShellOption">ShellOption</a></pre>

WithShellSense sets the wall sense (Inward, Outward or Centered). Without it the sense
is Inward (agent-docs/modify-design.md §8).

<a name="ShellSense"></a>
### type ShellSense

<pre>type ShellSense <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a></pre>

ShellSense is the wall sense of a shell (agent-docs/modify-design.md §8): the
thickness is a magnitude and carries no sign (core §8.1), so which way the
wall grows is enumerated, not signed.

<a name="Inward"></a><a name="Outward"></a><a name="Centered"></a>

<pre>const (
    // Inward grows the wall into the original solid; the outer skin does not
    // move. It is the default — what &#34;shell this box&#34; means everywhere.
    Inward <a href="#ShellSense">ShellSense</a> = iota
    // Outward grows the wall off the original solid; the original solid becomes
    // the cavity.
    Outward
    // Centered straddles the original surface, half the thickness each side. Only
    // a faceted solid whose faces all square to a world axis takes it
    // (agent-docs/orthogonal-design.md); any other body is ErrUnsupported.
    Centered
)</pre>

#### func WithSurfaceResult

<pre>func WithSurfaceResult() <a href="#SurfaceResultOption">SurfaceResultOption</a></pre>

SweepOption configures Sweep.

<a name="WithMitredJoins"></a>
#### func WithMitredJoins

<pre>func WithMitredJoins() <a href="#SweepOption">SweepOption</a></pre>

WithMitredJoins admits a [LineTo](<#LineTo>)-only path whose internal joins are corners:
the two spans meeting at a join are each cut on one join plane and share the
section polygon on it (agent-docs/sweep-design.md §16). The profile must be made
of straight lines only. Passing it twice is ErrDegenerate.

<a name="WithSectionScale"></a>
#### func WithSectionScale

<pre>func WithSectionScale(factors ...units.Value) <a href="#SweepOption">SweepOption</a></pre>

WithSectionScale states one dimensionless factor per path segment, in path
order: factors\[k\] is the ratio of the section at the END of span k to the
authored profile, so a branch whose radius is r\_k at path point k passes
r\_k / r\_0. Each factor must be a positive, finite Dimensionless value, and
the count must equal the path's segment count. On a path of two or more
spans it requires [WithMitredJoins](<#WithMitredJoins>) (agent-docs/sweep-design.md §16.2).

<a name="WithSweepTwist"></a>
#### func WithSweepTwist

<pre>func WithSweepTwist(angle units.Value) <a href="#SweepOption">SweepOption</a></pre>

WithSweepTwist rotates the profile about the path tangent as it travels.
A nonzero angle requires an origin XY sketch and a strictly convex whole-line
profile centred on the axis. [Section](<#Section>) 17 admits a positive-Z straight path
and a bounded line followed by a cardinal XZ quarter arc. Other cases
return ErrUnsupported without changing the document.

SweepReport states the first certified event or the earliest unresolved span.

<a name="SweepRequest"></a>
### type SweepRequest

<pre>type SweepRequest = report.<a href="report.md#SweepRequest">SweepRequest</a></pre>

SweepRequest bounds the time search and the contact geometry resolution.

RestSpeed is a nonnegative Velocity; the zero Value rests no vertex. A band
track over a support set (agent-docs/multibody-dynamics-design.md §10.5) holds a
lifted vertex that closes on the support plane no faster than RestSpeed, or
rises, on both sides of the plane, as it holds a contact vertex (§10.8), so
the track does not end where that vertex's lower height bound reaches the
plane. A departure rests nothing.

SweepSample keeps the query pose and the transferred pair finding.

SweepStartPolicy selects what to prove when the bodies initially touch.

<a name="SweptBox"></a>
### type SweptBox

<pre>type SweptBox struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}</pre>

SweptBox encloses every point a body occupies at any time of one pair path:
the body's Bounds() at its current placement, inflated by its Bound and
mapped exactly through the path's From, then expanded on every axis by the
path's whole-duration travel bound (agent-docs/contact-sweep-design.md §4.1). A
path that only translates takes the exact hull of its start and end boxes,
which holds every intermediate translate and lies inside that expansion.
Its extremes are exact dyadic rationals; agent-docs/multibody-dynamics-design.md
§4.2 owns it.

The zero value encloses nothing proven: it is never StrictlyDisjoint from
any box, and its [Box](<#Box>) is the zero [Box](<#Box>).

<a name="SweptBox.Box"></a>
#### func (SweptBox) Box

<pre>func (s <a href="#SweptBox">SweptBox</a>) Box() <a href="#Box">Box</a></pre>

[Box](<#Box>) converts the exact extremes outward: Min rounds down and Max rounds up,
so the float box contains the exact one. Bound is the largest conversion
step, and the box is Exact only when every extreme is a float.

StrictlyDisjoint reports a positive gap between s and o on at least one
axis, compared exactly. Boxes that merely meet are not disjoint.

<a name="WithVerification"></a>
#### func WithVerification

<pre>func WithVerification(v <a href="#Verification">Verification</a>) <a href="#TessellateOption">TessellateOption</a></pre>

WithVerification sets how much of the mesh's proof the call runs.

[Body.Tessellate](<#Body.Tessellate>) defaults to [VerifyAll](<#VerifyAll>). The export package's STL and OBJ
writers default to [VerifyNone](<#VerifyNone>) because they consume vertices and indices
without reading proof terms. Pass WithVerification([VerifyAll](<#VerifyAll>)) to demand
stronger proofs and accept their refusals.

A value naming none of the three levels is [ErrUnsupported](<#ErrUnsupported>).

<a name="TextArc"></a>
### type TextArc

<pre>type TextArc struct {
    Center    <a href="#Point2">Point2</a>
    Radius    units.Value
    Start     units.Value
    Clockwise <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#bool">bool</a>
}</pre>

TextArc is a circle to set lettering along. The baseline runs along the circle
of the given Radius about Center from the angle Start, which is measured
counter-clockwise from the plane's U axis. With Clockwise set the letters run
clockwise with their tops outward, as text reads along the top of a badge; with
it clear they run counter-clockwise with their tops inward, as it reads along
the bottom. Each letter keeps its own shape and is turned as a whole to stand
on the circle at the middle of its advance, so letters are not bent: a letter
much wider than the circle is large leaves a gap or a wedge between its
neighbours. Radius is a positive length and Start an angle. The lettering must
be one line.

<a name="TextSpec"></a>
### type TextSpec

<pre>type TextSpec struct {
    Text      <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a>
    Height    units.Value
    At        <a href="#Point2">Point2</a>
    Tolerance units.Value
    Font      []<a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#byte">byte</a>
    // Arc, when set, sets the first line along a circular arc instead of a
    // straight baseline (agent-docs/text-design.md §6). At is then unused.
    Arc *<a href="#TextArc">TextArc</a>
}</pre>

TextSpec describes a line of lettering for [TextProfiles](<#TextProfiles>).

Text is set in the font as written: runes of a line follow one another by the
font's advance widths with no kerning, and "\\n" starts the next line one line
height below. Height is the font size, the length of one em, a positive
length: a capital letter of the default font is about 0.7 of it tall. At is the
baseline's start of the first line in the sketch plane's coordinates. Tolerance
is optional: it is how far a flattened curve may lie from its polygon, a
positive length, and the zero units.Value means a thousandth of Height. Font is
optional TrueType font data, and nil sets the text in Go Regular.

ThickenSide names the side of the source sheet that receives material.
