<a name="ThreadForm"></a>
### type ThreadForm

<pre>type ThreadForm struct {
    Angle, Depth, Flat units.Value
    // FlankLead and FlankTrail, set in place of Angle, give an asymmetric groove,
    // a buttress thread&#39;s: each is the lean of a flank from the radial direction,
    // FlankLead of the flank toward the start of the face (its least position
    // along the axis) and FlankTrail of the one toward its far end. Each is an
    // angle above zero and below 90 degrees, and both must be set.
    FlankLead, FlankTrail units.Value
}</pre>

ThreadForm is a symmetric trapezoidal groove for [ThreadSpec.Form](<#ThreadSpec>). Angle is
the included angle between the two flanks, Depth how far the groove reaches
from the face to its root, and Flat the width of the root. The groove mouth
opens a twentieth of the pitch past the face, as the ISO groove's does. Set
all of Angle, Depth and Flat or none: the zero ThreadForm is the ISO profile.
Angle is an angle above zero and up to 120 degrees, and Depth and Flat are
positive lengths. FlankLead and FlankTrail take the place of Angle.

<a name="ThreadSize"></a>
### type ThreadSize

<pre>type ThreadSize struct {
    // Major is the thread&#39;s nominal (outside) diameter and Pitch its axial
    // advance per turn, both lengths.
    Major, Pitch units.Value
}</pre>

ThreadSize is a standard thread's major diameter and pitch, as [LookupThread](<#LookupThread>)
reads them from its designation.

<a name="LookupThread"></a>
#### func LookupThread

<pre>func LookupThread(designation <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#string">string</a>) (<a href="#ThreadSize">ThreadSize</a>, <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#error">error</a>)</pre>

LookupThread reads a thread designation into its major diameter and pitch
(agent-docs/thread-design.md §9). It reads five forms:

- "M10", an ISO metric thread at its coarse pitch: 10 mm and 1.5 mm. The
  nominal diameter is one of the preferred sizes from M1 to M64.
- "M10x1.25", a metric thread with the pitch stated, any positive pitch
  below the diameter.
- "1/4-20" and "1/4-28", and "1-8", a Unified thread by nominal fraction and
  threads per inch: 6.35 mm and 25.4/20 mm. The size is a multiple of 1/16 inch
  from 1/4 to 1 inch, and the threads per inch are its UNC or UNF value.
- "#10-24" and "#10-32", a Unified numbered size by its number and threads per
  inch: 0.190 inch and 25.4/24 mm. The size is #0 to #6, #8, #10 or #12, and the
  threads per inch are its UNC or UNF value.
- "G1/2", an ISO 228 parallel pipe thread by its nominal bore: 20.955 mm and 25.4/14 mm. The size is one of
  G1/8, G1/4, G3/8, G1/2, G5/8, G3/4, G7/8, G1, G1-1/4, G1-1/2 and G2. The size gives the diameter and pitch only:
  the thread's 55 degree Whitworth profile is not cut, and the caller picks the form.

The designation is case-insensitive in its M and x and takes no spaces. The
pitch is the thread's own and the major diameter is its nominal one: tolerance
classes, allowances and a thread's minor diameter are not read. A designation
that is none of these, or whose size is not in the tables, is ErrDegenerate.

<a name="ThreadSpec"></a>
### type ThreadSpec

<pre>type ThreadSpec struct {
    Face     <a href="#FaceSelector">FaceSelector</a>
    Pitch    units.Value
    LeftHand <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#bool">bool</a>
    Length   units.Value
    // Form is the groove&#39;s cross-section. The zero Form is the 60 degree ISO
    // basic profile; any other makes a symmetric trapezoidal groove, such as an
    // Acme or trapezoidal thread (agent-docs/thread-design.md §6).
    Form <a href="#ThreadForm">ThreadForm</a>
    // LeadIn, when set, is the distance of a 45 degree chamfer cut on each
    // convex end of the threaded face before the thread, so a screw or a nut
    // starts without a burr: a positive length (agent-docs/thread-design.md §7).
    LeadIn units.Value
    // LeadInAngle, set with LeadIn, is the angle between the lead-in&#39;s bevel and
    // the threaded face&#39;s end face, in place of 45 degrees: LeadIn stays the
    // bevel&#39;s distance along the end face and the bevel runs LeadIn·tan(angle)
    // along the threaded face. It is an angle above zero and below 90 degrees
    // (agent-docs/thread-design.md §10).
    LeadInAngle units.Value
}</pre>

ThreadSpec describes one ISO metric thread. [Face](<#Face>) selects the cylindrical face
to thread and must resolve to exactly one face. Pitch is the axial advance
per turn, a positive length.

The thread is right-handed unless LeftHand is set. Length is the axial length
to thread, measured from the end of the face with the least position along
the axis: the zero Value threads the whole face, and a positive length no
longer than the face stops the thread there, with the coil's flat end and no
runout (agent-docs/thread-design.md §5).

<a name="ThroughAll"></a>
### type ThroughAll

<pre>type ThroughAll struct {
    Dir <a href="#Direction">Direction</a> `json:&#34;dir&#34;`
}</pre>

ThroughAll sweeps in [Direction](<#Direction>) Dir to the farthest far side of every live
body with material beyond the sketch plane in the travel sense — the lateral
footprint is not consulted, so a body off to the side still counts. [Extent](<#Extent>)
only; each such body is resolved at the call and remains live
(agent-docs/evaluator-design.md §5).

<a name="ThroughAllSide"></a>
### type ThroughAllSide

<pre>type ThroughAllSide struct{}</pre>

ThroughAllSide is one side of a [TwoSided](<#TwoSided>) that runs to the farthest far side
of every live body with material beyond the sketch plane on this side, its
lateral footprint likewise not consulted. [SideExtent](<#SideExtent>) only.

<a name="ThroughHole"></a>
### type ThroughHole

<pre>type ThroughHole struct{}</pre>

ThroughHole runs the hole out of the far side of the body.

<a name="ToFace"></a>
### type ToFace

<pre>type ToFace struct {
    Body   *<a href="#Body">Body</a>
    Face   <a href="#FaceSelector">FaceSelector</a>
    Offset units.Value
}</pre>

ToFace stops the sweep at a face of [Body](<#Body>), displaced by the signed Offset —
the one signed number in the extent vocabulary: a positive offset
overshoots the face, a negative one stops short of it, so
ErrNegativeMagnitude does not apply (core §8.1/§12). A zero-value Offset
means no displacement. The sense of the sweep comes from the target face,
so ToFace carries no [Direction](<#Direction>). [Face](<#Face>) is a [FaceSelector](<#FaceSelector>), never a \*[Face](<#Face>)
(core §9), resolved as [Face](<#Face>).SelectFaces([Body](<#Body>)) under the implicit
exactly-one of core §12; [Body](<#Body>) must be a live body of the same document at
the call and is not consumed or retired. Both [Extent](<#Extent>) and [SideExtent](<#SideExtent>): a ToFace is a single
direction of travel, so it may also stand as one side of a [TwoSided](<#TwoSided>).

<a name="ToFaceAngular"></a>
### type ToFaceAngular

<pre>type ToFaceAngular struct {
    Body *<a href="#Body">Body</a>
    Face <a href="#FaceSelector">FaceSelector</a>
}</pre>

ToFaceAngular stops the revolve at a face of [Body](<#Body>) — the angular analog of
[ToFace](<#ToFace>), with no offset. The sense of the sweep comes from the target face
(a standalone ToFaceAngular takes the nearer way around; as a side of a
[TwoSidedAngle](<#TwoSidedAngle>) the side supplies the sense), so it carries no [Direction](<#Direction>).
[Face](<#Face>) is a [FaceSelector](<#FaceSelector>), never a \*[Face](<#Face>) (core §9), resolved as
[Face](<#Face>).SelectFaces([Body](<#Body>)) under the implicit exactly-one of core §12; [Body](<#Body>)
must be a live body of the same document at the call and is not consumed or
retired. Both
[AngularExtent](<#AngularExtent>) and [SideAngular](<#SideAngular>).

<a name="Verification"></a>
### type Verification

<pre>type Verification <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/builtin#int">int</a></pre>

Verification is how much of agent-docs/tessellation-design.md §1's proof
[Body.Tessellate](<#Body.Tessellate>) runs. It is an ORDERED level, because choosing how much
work to do is a total order: each level adds to the one below it.

What a mesh then PUBLISHES is two independent readings rather than a level
([Mesh.BoundaryVerified](<#Mesh.BoundaryVerified>), [Mesh.VolumeVerified](<#Mesh.VolumeVerified>)), because the proofs are not
a chain: a stitched body's occupied-volume proof rests on its vertices being
exact and its lumps proven separate rather than on more work, so a mesh can
carry one proof without the other, and a later proof may be independent of
the facet-contact audit rather than stronger than it.

<a name="VerifyNone"></a><a name="VerifyBoundary"></a><a name="VerifyAll"></a>

<pre>const (
    // VerifyNone asks for a mesh built to be drawn or exported rather than to
    // support a proof. The facet-contact audit, the area-slack proof and the
    // occupied-volume proof do not run, and the mesh states none of them:
    // [Mesh.BoundaryVerified] and [Mesh.VolumeVerified] are both false, and no
    // boolean composes such a mesh.
    //
    // Everything else holds unchanged. The mesh is chorded the same way, it
    // publishes the same proven [Mesh.Bound] and the same per-face
    // displacement behind it, it attributes the same source faces, it runs the
    // closed-mesh or manifold-with-boundary audit, the vertex-link audit, the
    // per-facet positive-area check and the signed-volume orientation audit,
    // and it is byte-for-byte the mesh a higher level builds — same vertices,
    // same indices, same order.
    VerifyNone <a href="#Verification">Verification</a> = iota
    // VerifyBoundary adds the facet-contact audit
    // (agent-docs/tessellation-design.md §9): no non-adjacent facet pair touches,
    // and an adjacent pair meets only along the vertex or edge its indices
    // share. That is what proves the facet set EMBEDDED, and so what makes
    // &#34;outside the body&#34; a geometric statement rather than the construction&#39;s
    // own convention ([Mesh.Triangles]). A mesh built here publishes
    // [Mesh.BoundaryVerified] true.
    VerifyBoundary
    // VerifyAll adds every proof the body&#39;s payload supports — the area slack
    // and, where the payload proves one, the occupied-volume bound that admits
    // the mesh to [Union], [Cut] and [Intersect]. It is the default, and it is
    // the only level any boolean accepts. A payload whose own occupied-volume
    // proof has not landed still publishes [Mesh.VolumeVerified] false here.
    VerifyAll
)</pre>

<a name="Vertex"></a>
### type Vertex

<pre>type Vertex struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}</pre>

Vertex is a topological point.

<a name="Vertex.Position"></a>
#### func (\*Vertex) Position

<pre>func (v *<a href="#Vertex">Vertex</a>) Position() <a href="#VecMeasurement">VecMeasurement</a></pre>

Position returns the vertex position in millimetres — a computed
coordinate, so it is bounded (core §6). A vertex read from a recorded
coordinate is Exact with a zero bound. A vertex at a COMPUTED coordinate
carries that computation's own proven displacement wherever the payload
tracks one: a boolean-built vertex carries the tessellation's chord bound;
a cap-loop chamfer's cap-level feet, which a float offset solve places
(agent-docs/modify-reach-design.md §8.4), carry that solve's own displacement; and
a PLACED loft's vertex, re-lifted from the record under a rigid motion,
carries that motion's own rounding (agent-docs/loft-design.md §5) — a recorded
coordinate the identity transform leaves alone is the zero-bound case of
that same rule, not an exception to it. An analytic prism's, revolve's,
cap-loop chamfer's, brep's or patch's own rim/junction/cap vertex carries
the rounding its own lift through the payload's frame and accumulated
placement committed, measured exactly for that vertex
(proofbound.ExactFrameLiftRound, revolvemesh.RevolveLift.SweptPointGap;
agent-docs/evaluator-design.md §8). A rim vertex where two recorded walks meet
also carries the bound that reaches the points BOTH walks denote there —
each walk's own end bound plus the gap between their held ends
(boundarywalk.JunctionVertex; agent-docs/evaluator-design.md §3) — so a cut
junction, a trimmed line end and a circle seam whose centre plus radius
rounds are never Exact. A revolve's vertex is measured against its
recorded plane point rotated about the recorded axis by the angle the
record states, so the same bound also covers the float axis coordinates it
was placed from, a radius snapped onto the axis, and the axis's own anchor
and direction error (agent-docs/evaluator-design.md §6). The frame origin is
part of that lift: a sketch plane whose axes are the world's own still
rounds origin.X + u whenever the sum is not representable, and a body built
far away and placed back keeps the far lift's rounding. A lift that is exact
for the coordinates at hand — an integer origin and integer coordinates
under the identity placement, for one — charges nothing.
A swept vertex is read from two independent coordinates and carries what each
was read from: its plane-local pair from the section, and its sweep level from
the extent. A level a [ToFace](<#ToFace>) or [ThroughAll](<#ThroughAll>) stop resolved in float, a magnitude
rescaled from a non-base unit, and a chamfered end's setback are all COMPUTED
levels, and each carries its own proven displacement into the vertex
(extrude.go's z0Delta/z1Delta). Being feature-built is not by itself a claim
of exactness: what the coordinate was READ FROM is.
